candidates.body:
## Idea

Closing the two test-coverage gaps found in #69
(`ValidationError::DuplicateNodeId`, the `validate_diagnostics` path) required
manually grepping every test function name against every enum variant and
cross-checking by hand. That works, but it's exactly the kind of exhaustive
check a tool should own — "mutation tests for every invariant" is a phrase
that shows up repeatedly across this session's task list (see #69, #71), and
each time it was verified by hand rather than by running an actual mutation
tester.

## Proposal

Add `cargo-mutants` (https://github.com/sourcefrog/cargo-mutants) as a
workspace dev tool, scoped first to `colorful-ir` (the crate with the most
invariant-heavy validation logic). Run it locally (and maybe as a non-blocking
CI job, since mutation runs are slow) to get a real "which mutants survived"
report instead of a manually-reasoned test inventory.

## Why it matters

A grep-based inventory only finds gaps in *existing* variant names — it can't
tell you that a check exists but is too weak (e.g. a range check that never
actually fires because of an earlier short-circuit). Real mutation testing
catches that class of bug; manual inventory doesn't.

No action requested beyond triage — flagging as a session takeaway per the
user's request.

## What changed

`main` at `401f8c1` is red on three required checks (`Rust dependency policy`,
`Editor integrations (compile)`, `Cargo package witness`) and on the advisory
`Current Rust stable` lane, so the ruleset blocks every open pull request. This
restores all four and carries the queued Dependabot branches as ordinary merge
commits, with the sibling edits Dependabot is not permitted to make.

Closes #334

| Check | Root cause | Change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Rust dependency policy` | `cargo-deny` rejects five advisories in the locked graphs: RUSTSEC-2026-0386 (`tokio` 1.53.1), RUSTSEC-2026-0414 and RUSTSEC-2026-0433 (`pulldown-cmark` 0.13.4), RUSTSEC-2026-0486 (`rustix` 1.1.4), RUSTSEC-2026-0592 (`url` 2.5.8). | `tokio` 1.54.1, `pulldown-cmark` `=0.13.6`, `rustix` 1.1.6, `url` 2.5.9 in every workspace that locks them (`29a3d72`). `deny.toml` gains no ignore. |

| `Cargo package witness` | `scripts/package-witness.sh` ran `cargo generate-lockfile` in the extracted workspace, so the packaged crates were checked against the newest compatible registry releases, not the reviewed `Cargo.lock`. When `js-sys` 0.3.107 was published, the packaged graph moved past the locked 0.3.103. `cargo check` only downloads host-relevant crates and `cargo fetch --locked` only caches the reviewed graph, so the packaged test's `cargo metadata --locked --offline` could not find the new target-gated crate. | The witness seeds the extracted workspace with the root `Cargo.lock` and asserts it is byte-identical before and after the locked check and test (`17726aa`). The lane is not a pull-request check; it was dispatched on this branch as run [45493834186](https://github.com/flyingrobots/colorful-language/actions/runs/45493834186). |

### Release admission

`validate-release` in `release.yml` runs `cargo test --all --locked` and the
package witness with no prior `cargo fetch --locked` and no restored cache.
That is the step sequence that failed in the stable lane (run 45492821476),
and a tag workflow cannot be repaired by rerunning the same tag, so `9704a5b`
adds the fetch before the v0.4.0 tag is cut. `check-release-distribution.mjs`
and its self-test accept the added step. This one is not verified by a run:
the tag workflow only runs on a `v*` tag.

### Dependabot branches

Merged with merge commits, so these pull requests land with this one: #320,
#321, #323, #331, #333 (single `editors/vscode` updates), #316 (root-node
group), #318 (github-actions group), #324 (cargo group).

Three updates inside those groups are held at their reviewed pins, each by a
follow-up commit, because a first-party self-test names the exact release and
raising it means changing a test expectation:

- #318: `ruby/setup-ruby` stays at v1.321.0 (`656a2a4`).

- #316: `mdast-util-from-markdown` stays at 2.0.3 and

  `scripts/check-roadmap-inventory.test.mjs` test `delegates roadmap Markdown

#324 moved `pulldown-cmark` only to 0.13.5, which still carries

Adds the terminal witness phase `abandoned`, named and specified on #387 (decision comment) for a public tag whose publication was abandoned, and moves the v0.4.0 witness to it with `v0.4.1` as its forward version, so a 0.4.1 target passes the predecessor rule.

## What changed

Build provenance attestation already shipped (`release.yml` `actions/attest`);
the bill-of-materials half did not. The tag workflow now generates an attested
CycloneDX SBOM for every release.

Closes #227

## Evidence

**Workflow.** `Install SBOM tool` pins `cargo-cyclonedx@0.5.9` through the
established `taiki-e/install-action` pattern (same reviewed SHA already used for
`cargo-mutants`, `cargo-llvm-cov`, `cargo-deny`, and `zizmor`). `Generate SBOM`
builds a CycloneDX document from the **locked** dependency graph into `dist/`,
so it publishes as a release asset via the existing `gh release create … dist/*`.
The SBOM is added to the `Attest Homebrew and editor artifacts` subject-path, so
it carries the same GitHub/Sigstore provenance as the bytes it describes.

**Ordering is load-bearing and enforced.** Generation runs *after* the native
archives are downloaded, so the dependency graph ships beside the artifacts it
covers, and *before* attestation, so it cannot be published unattested. Both
constraints are expressed in `REVIEWED_RELEASE_STEP_ORDER` rather than left to
convention.

**Policy.** `check-release-distribution.mjs` gains DIST-9 enforcement.
Deterministic mutations reject each refused shape:

| Mutation | Rejected because |
|---|---|
| generation step removed | no SBOM is produced |
| tool unpinned (`cargo-cyclonedx` with no version) | release inputs must be exact |
| output written outside `dist/` | asset would not publish |
| step reordered before the native download | graph would not describe shipped bytes |
| attestation omitting the SBOM | unattested artifact |

Two existing cases asserted the previous attestation message and are updated
**deliberately**, since the attested set genuinely changed — flagged rather than
quietly edited.

**Packet.** `docs/goalposts/v0.4.0/release.md` carries #227 in both *Must ship*
and *Scoped slices*; the validator's symmetric inventory admits **34** scoped
issues (was 33). ROADMAP moves #227 parked → delivered: it was parked pending
"the distribution and signing authorities", which #245 and #251 established.

**Gates.**

- `node --test scripts/check-release-distribution.test.mjs` — **33/33**, 0 fail.

  platforms, 3 editor registries.

The tag is immutable. An SBOM absent at tag time cannot be added to that

## What changed

Adopts the three queued major Cargo updates — `criterion` 0.8.2, `sha2` 0.11.0,
and `logos` 0.16.1 — in one reviewed change that also carries the first-party
source and sibling-lockfile edits a dependency-only Dependabot branch is not
permitted to make. Supersedes #274, #276, and #277, which are now closed.

Closes #285

## Evidence

This is a dependency adoption with two mechanical source fixes and one lockfile
resynchronization; there is no new behavior, so there is no planned/failing/
passing trio. Each commit is one independently reviewable dependency.

**`criterion` 0.5.1 → 0.8.2** (2afe81f). The crate no longer re-exports
`black_box` and `-D warnings` promotes the deprecation to a build failure, so
`crates/colorful-cli/benches/colorize_bench.rs` and
`crates/colorful-lsp/benches/semantic_tokens_bench.rs` now use
`std::hint::black_box` — the idiom
`crates/colorful-cli/examples/cross_stage_support/mod.rs` already used. No
script or workflow consumes criterion's report output, so nothing is coupled to
its measurement format; `scripts/release-profile-check.sh` uses the
`cross_stage_support` example instead. Verified at runtime with
`cargo bench -p colorful-cli --bench colorize_bench -- --test`.

**`sha2` 0.10.9 → 0.11.0** (37fee3b). Moves onto `digest` 0.11 and
`crypto-common` 0.2, replacing `generic-array` with `hybrid-array`. The digest
output no longer implements `LowerHex`, so the single `{:x}` site at
`crates/colorful-lsp/tests/lsp_envelope_report.rs:205` now uses the
byte-iteration idiom already used by
`crates/colorful-lsp/examples/lsp_envelope.rs`, producing the identical
lowercase hex string. The canonical hashing path was already immune, because
`sha256_hex` in `crates/colorful-ir/src/hashing.rs` iterates digest bytes rather
than relying on `LowerHex` — so `syntax_schema_hash`, `vocabulary_hash`, and
`build_hash` do not move. The resolved graph carries a single `digest` 0.11.3
and a single `crypto-common` 0.2.2, with no 0.10/0.11 split.

**`logos` 0.14.4 → 0.16.1** (ad3f724). Needs no source change: the derive,
`#[logos(skip ...)]`, `#[regex(...)]`, `Lexer::span`/`slice`/`source`/`bump`,
and the `Result`-yielding iterator are all unchanged. `beef` and `lazy_static`
leave the graph.

Because `crates/colorful-parse` is the lexer producing every downstream token
span, a compile-clean upgrade is not sufficient evidence — silent span drift
would alter canonical IR bytes without failing to build. Canonical IR was
therefore snapshotted with `colorful ir` across all 92 tracked prose corpora
before and after the bump. The outputs are identical per-file, aggregate
SHA-256:

```
c9873ceae5b5a11bb87224d137b50e19efbdf06ea34d30032f75ba0bccd4766a
```

The exhaustive `every_unicode_numeric_scalar_has_parser_lexicon_parity` case
still passes, covering the unmatched-scalar fall-through in
`extend_numeric_error` that initiates numeric tokens — the subtlest interaction
with logos' error path.

`fuzz/` is a separate workspace consuming `colorful-parse` by path, and
`.github/dependabot.yml` allows only `libfuzzer-sys` there, so Dependabot
structurally cannot synchronize `fuzz/Cargo.lock`. That is the actual cause of
the `--locked` failure on #277, before any lexer API question was reached. The
lockfile is resynchronized here, picking up `logos` 0.16.1 and `sha2` 0.11.0.

**Gates.**

- `cargo clippy --workspace --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings` — clean.
- `cargo test --workspace --locked` — all suites pass, zero failures.
- `cargo clippy --manifest-path fuzz/Cargo.toml --locked --bins -- -D warnings` — clean.
- `bash scripts/check-rust-dependency-policy.sh` — passes for all four
  workspaces; advisories, licenses, and sources ok.

  unviable, and zero survivors, packaged editor smoke, and 74 Markdown files

## What changed

`phf` moves from 0.11.3 to 0.14.0, together with the `fuzz/Cargo.lock`
synchronization that Dependabot structurally cannot carry. Closes #291.

This supersedes [#289](https://github.com/flyingrobots/colorful-language/pull/289),
which is red and cannot go green on its own: `.github/dependabot.yml` scopes
the `/fuzz` ecosystem to `allow: [libfuzzer-sys]`, so a Dependabot branch can
never resynchronize that sibling lockfile. Same structural reason that
superseded #277 with #286.

The macro surface is unchanged, so **no source edit was required**. That is the
finding, not the assumption — the Dependabot PR failed
`Rust dependency policy` with `cannot update the lock file fuzz/Cargo.lock
because --locked was passed`, before any API question was reached.

## Evidence

**Why a compile-clean upgrade is not sufficient.** `phf` is a direct workspace
dependency backing the three `phf_map!` static maps in
`crates/colorful-lexicon/src/lib.rs` — `FUNCTION_WORDS` (:38),
`OPEN_CLASS_WORDS` (:303), and `AMBIGUOUS_WORDS` (:410) — which classify every
word the parser sees. 0.14 replaces the generator's `rand` dependency with
`fastrand`, changing how the perfect hash is chosen. A classification or
map-iteration drift would alter canonical IR bytes without failing to build,
so it was measured rather than argued.

**Canonical IR is byte-identical.** `colorful ir` was run over all 73 tracked
Markdown corpora (`git ls-files '*.md'`) with a binary built at `main`
(`5ebde5e`, `phf` 0.11.3) and with this branch (`phf` 0.14.0). Per-file
SHA-256 digests are identical for every file. No output was empty — no digest
equals the SHA-256 of zero bytes (checked directly; distinctness would *not*
have shown this, since a single empty output still leaves 73 distinct
digests). The corpus is pinned at `5ebde5e` and paths are repo-relative from
the repository root, because `colorful ir` embeds the path it is given and
because `CHANGELOG.md` is itself one of the 73 inputs. Hashing the sorted
`<path>` + two spaces + `<digest>` manifest gives
`e632761224da0cbb3204ef11ce48b843377ec15b8617148e7b61c2ba50e52cd0` on both
sides. The baseline was produced from a clean `git worktree` at `main`, not
from a mutated tree.

**Gates.**

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo clippy --workspace --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |
| `cargo test --workspace --locked` | 0 failures |
| `cargo check --manifest-path fuzz/Cargo.toml --locked --bins` | clean |
| `cargo fmt --all -- --check` (root and `fuzz`) | clean |
| `bash scripts/check-rust-dependency-policy.sh` | 4 workspaces; advisories, licenses, sources ok |
| `bash scripts/check-generated-vocabulary-drift.sh` | passed (schema authority only — **not** evidence for the lexicon maps; see below) |
| `cargo test -p colorful-lexicon --locked` | 18 passed, 0 failed (includes the two new `phf` invariants) |
| `bash scripts/check-generated-ir-drift.sh` | passed |
| `node scripts/check-roadmap-inventory.mjs` | 58 primary markers structurally valid |

**Correction (was wrong in the first revision, now enforced).** An earlier
revision of this PR cited `check-generated-vocabulary-drift.sh` as covering
`phf` map-iteration order. It does not and cannot: its generator reads exactly
one authority, `contracts/colorful/vocabulary.v1.schema.json`
(`generate-vocabulary-validators.mjs:8`), and never reads, compiles, or
executes `crates/colorful-lexicon`. Falsified by injecting a fabricated
`FUNCTION_WORDS` entry — the drift check still exits 0 and reports "passed".
Caught by @chatgpt-codex-connector.

Two things replace that claim, in `20edd45`:

- `every_phf_entry_resolves_to_its_own_value` walks each table's own entries
  and requires the public `get` path to return that same entry. Every previous
  lexicon test reached these tables only through the handful of keys it named,
  so a generator that mislaid an unnamed key went unnoticed. Verified live by
  pinning one lookup to a constant key, which fails per-entry.
- `phf_iteration_visits_every_entry` compares the trip count against the
  compile-time `len`, so neither loop can pass vacuously.

Map *iteration* order is unobservable rather than merely unchanged: outside
those two tests, no code iterates these tables — only `get` and `len`.

**Licensing.** `fastrand` enters the graph and `rand`/`rand_core` leave it;
`check-rust-dependency-policy.sh` reports `licenses ok` across all four
workspaces. No Apache-2.0 incompatibility.

This is a dependency adoption, not a behavior change, so there is no
planned/failing/passing trio — the existing suite is the spec, and no test was
relaxed, skipped, or altered.

`v0.4.0` turns Colorful's post-`v0.3.0` hardening campaign into one coherent
public promise: a deterministic prose-analysis core whose public adapters fail
closed on malformed coordinates and contracts, whose LSP remains fresh under
reviewed document loads, and whose native and editor artifacts can be built,
checked, attested, installed, and rolled back through a documented release
path.

The release favors evidenced product maturity over speculative depth. It
retains the moonshot architecture and compatibility boundaries, while shipping

## Version decision

  editor/distribution surfaces gain new public behavior.

- Add a repeated or otherwise forced ordering test that fails against the current race and passes without timing luck.
- Update the owning external-analyzer test plan and current reference after the executable evidence is green.
- Run the complete release-preparation gate and demonstrate that the test remains stable under concurrent suite load.

## Classification

## Smell

`scripts/check-roadmap-inventory.mjs` now contains 1,429 lines and 34 top-level helpers that collectively recognize enough CommonMark/GFM structure to decide which `ROADMAP.md` heading and table are authoritative. The implementation was hardened through a long sequence of boundary-specific fixes for comments, raw HTML, fences, inline code, styled headings, malformed tables, and paragraph continuations.

Issue #187 correctly made roadmap ownership deterministic. Issue #243 correctly made architecture-accountability rows unique. This follow-up owns the maintainability debt created by making a repository policy checker responsible for a bespoke Markdown parser.

## Why it matters

The gate is fail-closed and security-sensitive: a parser disagreement can either reject an honest roadmap or let visually misleading structure bypass the accountability contract. Continuing to reproduce CommonMark semantics locally expands the review surface and makes each documentation edge case a new parser feature.

## Proposed direction

Preserve the existing policy and deterministic diagnostics while moving structural recognition to one explicit authority:

- Prefer a small, checked-in machine-readable accountability manifest that generates or verifies the relevant roadmap table; or
- use a maintained Markdown event parser whose version and interpretation are pinned and fixture-tested.

Do not weaken the current fail-closed behavior merely to reduce line count.

## Acceptance criteria

- Add characterization evidence for every currently supported roadmap fixture before changing the parser boundary.
- Keep all existing live-inventory, mutation, duplicate-row, malformed-structure, and path-addressed diagnostic cases green.
- Establish one canonical source for primary issue disposition and architecture-accountability identities.
- Detect drift between the canonical source and the human-readable `ROADMAP.md` deterministically and offline.
- Remove the bespoke block/inline Markdown state machine only after byte-for-byte or explicitly reviewed diagnostic parity.
- Record the before/after maintained source size and parser responsibility; the change must reduce custom parsing surface rather than relocate it.
- Update `docs/topics/project-governance/test-plan.md` and its current reference with the resulting authority boundary.

## Evidence

<!-- Keep the contract honest: code, docs, and evidence should agree on `main`. -->

## What changed

Adds a manual `workflow_dispatch` dry run to `.github/workflows/release.yml`, keyed on the event, that runs admission, the three native builds, packaging, and the checks on the assembled artifact set without reaching any step that has an effect outside the run. A tag run still reaches every publication step.

Closes #374


## Release workflow step map (on `origin/main` before this change)

Trigger today: `push` of a `v*` tag only. Workflow-level `permissions: {}`. Concurrency group `release-${{ github.ref }}`.

### Job `validate-release` ("Validate release admission"), `contents: read`

| Step | Outside effect | Reads tag context |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `actions/checkout` (full history, no persisted credentials) | no | checks out `github.ref` |
| `actions/setup-node` | no | no |
| `dtolnay/rust-toolchain` 1.97.1 | no | no |
| Install repository policy dependencies (`npm ci`) | no (registry download) | no |
| Verify release metadata | no | `version="${GITHUB_REF_NAME#v}"`; compares to `Cargo.toml` `[workspace.package]` version; `CHANGELOG.md` `## [$version]`; `docs/goalposts/${GITHUB_REF_NAME}/release.md` and `verification.md` |
| Verify the tag is on main | no | `git rev-parse "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}^{commit}"`, ancestor of `origin/main` |
| Check release profile | no | no |
| Self-test release packet policy | no | no |
| Check release packet | no | indirectly: resolves tags from history |
| Check editor version compatibility | no | no |
| Check release distribution policy | no | no |
| Self-test Homebrew formula generation | no | no |
| Cache the whole locked dependency graph | no | no |
| Validate Rust formatting / lints / tests / release build | no | no |
| Validate package witness | no | no |

### Job `binary-artifacts` ("Native binaries", 3-target matrix), `contents: read`, `id-token: write`, `attestations: write`

| Step | Outside effect | Reads tag context |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `actions/checkout` | no | `github.ref` |
| `dtolnay/rust-toolchain` | no | no |
| Build native binaries | no | no |
| Package native binaries | no | `dist_name="colorful-language-${GITHUB_REF_NAME}-${TARGET}"` |
| Attest native archive (`actions/attest`) | **yes**: public Sigstore and GitHub attestation records | subject is the tag-named archive |
| Upload native archive (`actions/upload-artifact`) | run-scoped artifact only, 7-day retention | artifact name from target only |

### Job `release` ("Build and publish release"), `contents: write`, `id-token: write`, `attestations: write`

| Step | Outside effect | Reads tag context |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `actions/checkout`, `actions/setup-node`, `dtolnay/rust-toolchain` | no | `github.ref` |
| Set up formula syntax Ruby | no | no |
| Install repository policy dependencies / editor packaging dependencies | no | no |
| Download native archives | no (run artifacts) | no |
| Install SBOM tool | no | no |
| Generate SBOM | no | file names use `${GITHUB_REF_NAME}` |
| Generate Homebrew formula | no | `version="${GITHUB_REF_NAME#v}"` |
| Build and smoke editor packages | no | `version="${GITHUB_REF_NAME#v}"`; Zed archive name uses `${GITHUB_REF_NAME}` |
| Attest Homebrew and editor artifacts | **yes**: public attestation records | no |
| Publish to crates.io (`CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN`) | **yes**: crates.io publication | `version="${GITHUB_REF_NAME#v}"` |
| Create GitHub Release (`GH_TOKEN: github.token`) | **yes**: public release and assets | `gh release create "$GITHUB_REF_NAME"`; notes path |
| Verify GitHub Release VSIX | **yes** (reads the public release asset; meaningless without one) | `version="${GITHUB_REF_NAME#v}"` |

## Design

- **Trigger.** `workflow_dispatch` with no inputs. The dry-run mode is the event (`github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'`); no free-form input selects it, so a tag push cannot.
- **What a dry run skips.** Exactly five steps carry `if: github.event_name == 'push'`: `Attest native archive`, `Attest Homebrew and editor artifacts`, `Publish to crates.io`, `Create GitHub Release`, `Verify GitHub Release VSIX`. No job carries a condition and no other step does, so a tag run executes exactly the steps it executed before.
- **What a dry run runs.** All of `validate-release`; in each native matrix job, build, package, checksum, and `Upload native archive` (a run artifact, 7-day retention); in `release`, setup, dependency installs, `Download native archives`, `Install SBOM tool`, `Generate SBOM`, `Generate Homebrew formula` (with `ruby -c`), `Build and smoke editor packages`.
- **Version.** `Verify release metadata` now selects the release tag by event: `push) release_tag="$GITHUB_REF_NAME"`; `workflow_dispatch) release_tag="v${workspace_version}"`, where `workspace_version` is the same `awk` read of `Cargo.toml` `[workspace.package]` the step already did. The comparison with the workspace version, the `CHANGELOG.md` section, and both packet files are unchanged and still apply to a tag run. The step writes `release_tag` to `GITHUB_OUTPUT`; the job exports it as `release-tag`; the native and release jobs set `RELEASE_TAG` from it, and the packaging steps (`Package native binaries`, `Generate SBOM`, `Generate Homebrew formula`, `Build and smoke editor packages`) name artifacts from `RELEASE_TAG`. On a tag run `RELEASE_TAG` equals `GITHUB_REF_NAME`. The tag-only publication steps are unchanged and still read `GITHUB_REF_NAME`.
- **Non-main refusal.** `Verify release metadata` exits 1 for a dispatch whose `GITHUB_REF` is not `refs/heads/main` (this also refuses a dispatch on a tag ref). `Verify the tag is on main` checks `"${GITHUB_REF_NAME}^{commit}"` on a tag run, as before, and `"${GITHUB_SHA}^{commit}"` on a dry run, against `origin/main`. The refusal binds this reviewed workflow file; a branch that edits its own copy of the workflow is outside what any check in this file can bound.
- **Attestation: skipped in a dry run.** GitHub permits attesta

## Summary

Implements Issue #1 — the domain foundation for the Synapse P2P inference protocol: identity primitives (NodeId, KeyPair, Node), model primitives (ModelId, ExpertId, Catalog), shared kernel (DomainError, DomainEvent), and application ports (KeySigner, IdentityStore) plus the Ed25519Signer infrastructure adapter.

## Changes

**Shared Kernel** — 2 files
- `shared/domain_error.rs`: 16 variants, thiserror derives, 9 tests
- `shared/domain_event.rs`: 7 variants with UUIDs for idempotency, serde roundtrip, 5 tests

**Identity Module** — 7 files
- `identity/node_id.rs`: SHA256 of Ed25519 pubkey, hex parsing, Display, 13 tests
- `identity/key_pair.rs`: Pure domain entity (rand, no ed25519-dalek), 6 tests
- `identity/node.rs`: Aggregate with register/reputation/events, 15 tests
- `identity/ports.rs`: KeySigner + IdentityStore traits, 5 contract tests
- `identity/infrastructure/ed25519_signer.rs`: Ed25519 adapter (only file with ed25519-dalek), 7 tests
- Domain layer purity enforced: zero I/O, zero crypto deps outside infrastructure/

**Model Module** — 4 files
- `model/model_id.rs`: Non-empty + kebab-case validation, 15 tests
- `model/expert_id.rs`: Composite VO with bounds checking, 10 tests
- `model/model_entity.rs`: Full 12-field production schema
- `model/catalog.rs`: Aggregate with register/list/find/remove + DomainEvents, 10 tests
- Gateway `GET /v1/models` wired to domain Catalog

**Documentation**
- AGENTS.md with Non-Negotiable Design Principles (DDD + Clean Architecture + TDD)
- ADRs 0001-0010: Rust, MoE-only, libp2p, DDD/Clean Architecture, NodeId, vLLM, single binary, two swarm modes, axum, Solidity L2 staking
- Architecture doc with Mermaid diagrams: `docs/architecture/identity-module.md`

## Acceptance
- ✅ `cargo test`: 114/114 passed
- ✅ `cargo clippy -- -D warnings`: clean

- ✅ Domain layer has zero external dependencies
- ✅ All public types documented with doc comments

Bumps [jsdom](https://github.com/jsdom/jsdom) from 30.0.1 to 30.1.1.
Release notes

Sourced from jsdom's releases.

v30.1.1

  • Fixed spurious window blur and focusout events and incorrect event.relatedTarget values when focusing an element after removing the previously focused element, which regressed in v30.1.0. (@​asamuzaK)
  • Fixed focus and blur behavior across frames, and focusing the document's viewport through document.documentElement.focus(). (@​asamuzaK)
  • Fixed focus targets removed or disabled by blur listeners becoming active, and text selections made by focus and blur listeners being overwritten. (@​asamuzaK)
  • Fixed element.focus() incorrectly focusing disabled form controls and <input type="hidden"> elements with tabindex="". (@​scttcper)
  • Fixed invalid style.setProperty() calls changing existing !important priorities, serialized styles, or mutation records. (@​FedgeNo)
  • Fixed !important handling when updating CSS longhands after shorthands, using variables or CSS-wide keywords, and assigning style properties directly. (@​FedgeNo)
  • Fixed <noscript> parsing with includeNodeLocations: true or inside frames to honor the runScripts option.
  • Fixed the storageQuota option being ignored by frames.
  • Fixed encoding detection of HTML and XML byte input to honor XML encoding declarations and detect UTF-16 without a byte order mark.
  • Fixed exceptions caused by truncated charset parameters in <meta> elements, and encoding detection incorrectly using incomplete <meta> tags. (@​FedgeNo)
  • Fixed XML serialization errors for namespaces named constructor, toString, __proto__, or "null", and incorrect reuse of namespace prefixes declared on sibling elements.
  • Fixed element.innerHTML and element.outerHTML in XML documents to reject invalid characters in attribute values and avoid stack overflows on large strings.
  • Fixed selector matching for :lang(), :nth-child(... of ...) after mutations, and :has() with duplicate IDs or nested logical pseudo-classes. (@​asamuzaK)

v30.1.0

jsdom is feeling the AGI!

This release is dedicated to @​scttcper, who unleashed @​codex upon jsdom and found tons of performance improvements. Along the way, he found and fixed many correctness issues as well.

We really appreciate his thoughtful PRs, which did a great job following the project's contribution guidelines, and were clearly human-curated, with their PR descriptions edited to be brief and respectful of the maintainers' time.

Thanks to @​scttcper, as well as all the other contributors of this release (most of whom were AI-assisted).

  • Added named access to elements on document, such as document.myForm for <form name="myForm">. (@​vojtisprime11)
  • Added QuotaExceededError, including its use for storage quota errors and oversized crypto.getRandomValues() requests.
  • Added support for the relaxed DOM naming rules when creating elements, attributes, and document types.
  • Improved performance of DOM construction, tree mutations, range operations, and live collection access, especially on large documents. (@​scttcper, @​erezrokah)
  • Improved performance of getComputedStyle(), style changes, and CSS serialization. (@​scttcper, @​jhult)
  • Improved performance of event dispatch, form control and label lookups, and updates to <select> elements and radio button groups. (@​scttcper)
  • Reduced memory use when creating and working with DOM nodes, attributes, event listeners, and mutation observers. (@​scttcper)
  • Changed window.close() to preserve access to the document and its DOM through retained references.
  • Fixed element.querySelectorAll() returning no matches when the first part of the selector matches the element itself, which regressed in v30.0.0. (@​asamuzaK)
  • Fixed case sensitivity in CSS attribute selectors, including selectors matching data-state="", title="", and other case-sensitive values. (@​asamuzaK)
  • Fixed document.querySelector() failing to find a matching element when an earlier element has the same ID

One workflow, `ci.yml`, with the four PR checks:
- `go`: build, lint, test, coverage of the changed lines;
- `docs`: skills, markdown budgets, manifests;
- `fuzz`: 45 s per target of the changed packages;
- `mutate`: gremlins on the changed lines, advisory.

`skills.yml`, `fuzz.yml` and `mutation.yml` are folded in. A push to `main` reruns `go` and `docs`.

- **The nightly fuzz is dropped.** It re-fuzzed rarely changed code for 5 min per target; the only bug fuzzing found came from a PR run.
- **`bench.yml` is dropped.** It ran once; `docs/benchmarks.md` keeps the local commands.
- **`release.yml` and `badges.yml` are unchanged.** `badges` is scheduled hourly, and GitHub runs it every few hours.

This PR runs the new workflow itself.

## What failed, or what was missing

A custom techset written while the MCP server was running wasn't a material type for it: `gdt_edit` and `gdt_check` said `no techsetdef for material type "t7dxbc_test" — APE shows INVALID MATERIAL TYPE` and `gdt_schema` errored, while the CLI (a fresh process) accepted the same material. The server indexed the techsetdef tree once, at its first GDT call, and never again; an edited techsetdef also kept its old texture slots.

## The change

`internal/gdt`'s techset index now stays fresh, as the GDT index already did:

- a material type it doesn't know rescans the tree, at most every 2 s (a GDT full of misspelt types doesn't walk it per asset);
- the tree is rescanned once it is two minutes old, which is how a deleted techsetdef goes;
- a resolved techset remembers the files it read (the techsetdef and its `#include`s) with their time and size, and is read again when one changed (checked at most every 5 s).

A rescan swaps the whole tree atomically, so parallel MCP handlers never see a half-built one. The package doc says how the tree stays fresh.

## How it was verified

- Found on a real session: creating `t7dxbc_test.techsetdef` under `share/raw/techsetdefs_stable/geometry/` for the t7dxbc in-game test, `gdt_edit` refused the material until the CLI was used instead.
- New tests (`techset_fresh_test.go`): a new techsetdef found after a rescan and not before the rate limit; an edited techsetdef and an edited include read again, by time alone and by size alone; a deleted one forgotten (at once once resolved, after the walk period otherwise) and rescanning once, not per lookup; a known type never rescanning; a failed rescan keeping its tree; a missing root an error; a material type winning over an include of the same name in either walk order; parallel lookups during rescans.
- Mutation testing (go-mutesting, 240 mutants of `techset.go`): every mutant on the changed lines is killed except these, which change nothing observable:
  - `rescanEvery` 1 s or 3 s instead of 2 s, and `<` instead of `<=` at the edge of the rescan window, the two-minute walk period or the restat window (gremlins: `techset.go` 136, 149, 218): tuning of the rate limits;
  - the restat window measured from 1 s earlier: the same;
  - not recording when the files were last found unchanged: the files are statted on every lookup past the window instead of once per window, a cost only;
  - removing `scanMu.Unlock()` deadlocks the tests, a timeout.
- `go test ./...` and `golangci-lint` clean.

## Checklist

- [x] No personal paths, private map content, or credentials in the diff
- [x] No skill or plugin change

## What was missing

The user reads no diffs: the tests are the review. CI only ran `go test`, which replays the fuzz seeds but never fuzzes, says nothing of mutation, and lets a PR land with code no test runs.

## The change

- **`ci.yml`** — tests run with `-coverpkg=./...`; a PR **fails** unless 80% of its changed Go lines ran under test (`.github/scripts/patch_coverage.py`, uncovered lines listed in the job summary).
- **`mutation.yml`** — gremlins v0.6.0 on the PR's changed lines, **advisory** (the approach Google describes: diff-only, surfaced for review, no suppression list). Lived mutants and changed lines no test runs go to the job summary, `gremlins.json` to an artifact; `workflow_dispatch` mutates the diff from any ref.
- **`fuzz.yml`** — 45 s per Fuzz target of the PR's changed packages; every target 5 min nightly; a failing input fails the job and is uploaded.
- **`CLAUDE.md`** — one bullet on what each check asks of a contributor.

## How it was verified

- `patch_coverage.py` on past release ranges, in CI conditions (no BO3 install, no real db): 2.4→2.5 77.0%, 2.5→2.6 80.0%, 2.6→2.7.0 64.9%, 2.7.0→2.7.1 100%, 2.7.1→main 94.2%. Fails under its minimum (exit 1), passes with no changed Go line.
- gremlins on Linux (WSL, Go 1.25.5) over the 2.7.1→main diff: 104 killed, 13 lived, 7 not covered, 46 s, identical on a second run with `GOFLAGS=-count=1` (without it, a cached coverage run made 79 of 124 mutants time out). `mutation_report.py` rendered that output, a missing file and an empty diff.
- `fuzz.sh` with `BASE=v2.7.1`: fuzzes only `xpak` and `gdt`; with a planted failure it exits 1, annotates, and Go keeps the input under `testdata/fuzz/FuzzRead/`.
- `actionlint` 1.7.7: clean. A throwaway draft PR with an untested Go function exercises the three jobs on a real diff (linked below once it ran).

candidates.body:
A new tool reads the game's log when something goes wrong in game: `game_log` (MCP), `t7kb game log` (CLI). Closes #66: the dialog half shipped in #70, and this is the log half.

The first version of this PR read the log at the end of the run's 90-second watch. That moment has nothing to do with when problems appear:

- a quick map has loaded in about 25 s, and the wait is wasted;
- a big map is still loading when the watch ends;
- a mod's run only reaches the menu;
- anything that goes wrong while the mapper plays comes after the watch.

So the run now only makes the game write a log, and the agent reads it when the user reports a problem.

## `game_log`

- **Which file.** It picks the current `console_mp.log`: for a map or mod name, the newer of `mods/<name>/` and the game root; otherwise the newest of all. The answer also lists every other log beside it, newest first: other `console_mp.log`s, `crashes.log` and `console.log`.
- **What it sorts.** The last launch (after the last `logfile opened on`) is sorted into:
  - **script errors**: the S.R.E. block, with its message and call stack frames;
  - **the map's own problems**: lookups that failed for assets its zone (or the mod's zones) lists, and Error lines of any other kind;
  - **stock lookups**: the failed lookups every load prints, counted by type (about 220 on a stock template).
- **Line numbers.** Every finding carries its line number in the file. The answer also gives the lines of each map load (`Game Initialization`) and of `ModLoad done: <map>`.
- **Raw lines.** `grep` (case-insensitive RE2, with `context` lines and a `max`, the rest counted) and `tail`. When the sorting misses the symptom, the agent can read around a line in the file itself, as the description tells it to. `path` reads a log the agent names.

The rules (which file, which lines, what counts as the map's) are in `internal/gamelog/doc.go`.

## The run stage

- It starts the game with `logfile 2` unless the run sets `logfile`, and watches only its start (see the watcher above).
- Its note names the log it wrote (`log: …\console_mp.log (game_log reads it)`), or says it wrote none.
- The dialog detection from #70 is unchanged.

## Docs

- The skills: compiling routes to `game_log`. Debugging says `game_log` reads the log, and that its sorting is a first pass to read around. Debugging's `[ms][TAG]` prefix line is corrected: the prefix appears only while `developer` is on.
- `docs/cli/build.md` has a `game log` section.
- The README diagram, `CLAUDE.md`'s run surfaces and the skill validator's tool list include it.

## The watcher: the agent hears of each problem as it happens

`t7kb game watch` follows the game's logs and processes and prints one line per problem:
- a script error, once per launch, with the file's line;
- a fatal error;
- a dialog the game shows, unless it repeats a fatal error the log already said;
- a process that ended with an error code;
- once a map has loaded, the assets its zone lists that the game didn't find.

It follows every launch and every reload from the game's console (`devmap`, `map_restart`). It never prints stock noise, and prints at most 20 lines per launch.

The plugin runs it as a **plugin monitor** (`plugin/monitors/monitors.json`) for the whole Claude Code session, so each line reaches the agent as a notification. `game_log` remains the investigation tool and gains:
- `after`: read only what is new since an earlier answer;
- `dialogs`: the dialogs the running game shows.

Together they give clients without monitors the same stream, on demand.

The build's run now watches only the game's start (8 s): a dialog, or the game quitting at once, still fails the run. The 90-second watch is gone: it ended too early for a big map, wasted time on a small one, and missed everything after it. Builds and Radiant can feed the same channel later: #101.

**Verified:**
- **Live through Claude Code's Monitor tool:** I launched a game without Steam. The watcher notified its dialog ("Vous devez lancer Steam pour jouer à ce jeu"), and said nothing when the game then closed cleanly.
- **Two real logs, replayed the way the game writes them** (in chunks, then rewritten by a new launch):
  - the script error came once, at line 3347, with the GSC's lines 77 and 72;
  - then the fatal zone error at line 1088.
- **Plugin:** `claude plugin validate` passes with the monitor.

## Verified on real logs

| Log | Result |
| --- | --- |
| the install's current one, a stock template load | 237 stock lookups counted, nothing else; the 5 other logs listed |
| a run with a deliberate `if ( undefined )` in the map's GSC | `script error: cannot cast undefined to bool \| file 'scripts/zm/zm_t7kb_noise.gsc', line 77 :: \| … line 72 :: \| …` at line 3349 |
| a map the French game refused (English-only link) | `Com_ERROR: ERROR: Could not find zone 'fr_zm_t7kb_noise'` at line 1088, found by `--grep "could not find zone"` with its context |

Each run was closed without force, and the install was restored afterwards.

## Tests

- **`internal/gamelog`:**
  - the last launch with the file's line numbers;
  - sorting with and without a map;
  - an unclosed or long script error;
  - grep context and caps, and tail;
  - `Find` with and without a name;
  - `Written` and `Zoned`;
  - `FuzzSort`.
- **`internal/cli`:** the operation over a game root fixture (usermap, mod, path, caps, errors), the MCP handler and the command.
- **`internal/build`:** `withGameLog`, the note, and a pipeline case.

New code coverage is 100%, except for the open error after a stat.

Part of #20: the two levers that shrink a map's upload without cutting content, each measured on real links.

## What failed, or what was missing

- A map's `.xpak` only grows: the linker appends what changed and leaves the data it replaced in the file, read by nothing — and the Launcher's Publish uploads the whole `usermaps/<map>/zone/` folder as it is. Nothing told a modder how much of their upload is dead data, and the Launcher has no way to rewrite the `.xpak`.
- #20's oversized-texture lever was unverified: does `mipBase` really cut an image, by how much, and which images are worth it?

## The change

- **`build fresh_xpak`** (CLI `--fresh-xpak`): the link stage sets every `.xpak` in the target's `zone/` aside, keeps each one the link writes anew, and puts back the others (languages this link didn't build); a failed link gets every old file back. The stage note gives the sizes before and after.
- **`zone_contents` without a line** adds `upload`: the bytes of the `zone/` folder, a lower bound on the `.xpak` data no entry reads, and, once that is 1% of the `.xpak` bytes, the advice to link the published build fresh. A new `internal/format/xpak` reads a `.xpak`'s index (header, 24-byte entries: key, offset, size).
- **`zone_contents images`** (CLI `--images`), for the whole build or a zone line: images by who defines them (your GDTs, stock, none), then your GDTs and largest images by what one `mipBase` step down would save, with each image's `mipBase`, GDT and zone line. `doNotResize` and `1/8` images save nothing; an image defined in two GDTs says so.
- **`t7kb:compiling`**: a section on publishing (link fresh, then `mipBase`), a description that triggers on a huge published map or a growing `.xpak`, a new eval case; the `t7kb build` shell fallback moves whole to `references/cli.md` (the body was over its aim).
- `internal/gdt/doc.go`: gdt.db is readable after `PRAGMA writable_schema=ON` (except `weaponcamo` and `scriptbundle`, wider than SQLite's 2,000-column limit); what keeps it from replacing the index is freshness.

## How it was verified

- **Dead `.xpak` data**: deleting `zm_init_sample_map.xpak` and relinking took it from 95.3 to 89.0 MB, with the same assets and sizes in the report. In freshly linked files every gap between entries is padding up to a power of two of at most 32 KiB, so anything past that boundary is dead; on the dirty file the measure counts 5.9 of the 6.29 MB the fresh link dropped (the rest: replaced entries whose keys stay in the table). Every `.xpak` in the install reads with entries inside the data and none overlapping (`TestInstallXpaks`, opt-in with `TA_TOOLS_PATH`); `FuzzRead` ran 30 s clean.
- **What Publish uploads**: the Launcher builds its Workshop content path as `%1/%2/zone` and reads `workshop.json` from it (strings in `bin/modlauncher.exe`).
- **`fresh_xpak`**: fake-linker tests (map, mod, failed link, interrupted run, option off) and a real link (90.7 → 89.3 MB; `en_*.xpak` rewritten byte for byte, `fr_*.xpak` kept).
- **`mipBase`**: on fresh links, a 4K colour map streams 22.4 MB at `1/1`, 5.6 at `1/2`, 1.4 at `1/4`, resident part unchanged; image data leaves the `.xpak` byte for byte (it doesn't compress). Stepping 13 images of 0.7–22 MB down at once with `gdt_edit`: **62,390,244 bytes predicted, 62,390,272 saved** in the report, the `.xpak` 62.8 MB smaller, no other asset changed. Per image the estimate is within 5%.
- On a real 10.2 GB upload: at least 156 MB of dead `.xpak` data, and one step on the map's own images would take ~4.76 GB of 6.67 GB.
- Each commit builds and passes its tests on its own; `go test ./...`, `go vet`, `golangci-lint` clean. Token report: `zone_contents` whole map 1243 → 1317, `images` 1320 (map) / 1185 (line); `docs/benchmarks.md` updated. The new eval case and the two compiling cases the rewording touched fire (one run each).

Not in this PR (still open in #20): unused content, and the ~1.3 GB of that upload outside the `.xpak` (mostly `zone/snd/`).

## Checklist

- [x] `python plugin/skills/contribute/scripts/check_skills.py` reports 0 errors
- [x] No personal paths, private map content, or credentials in the diff
- [x] Description still under 1,024 characters, no `<tags>`, third person — and a trigger case in `plugin/evals/` added or adjusted if it changed

Part of #51. Needs M0 (McReaper/t7_radiant_bridge#1).

The agent edits the map open in the user's Radiant directly, and each agent action is one labelled undo step ("t7kb: …"). This milestone measures whether the agent's blockouts are worth the sandbox and the pull pane (M1b).

## Plugin (t7_radiant_bridge)

The pipe server; read entities and the selection; import, delete and set keys with undo; select by GUID; trigger a command on a selection; get and set the camera; capture a view; console lines; save and reload; events (map loaded or saved, prefab scope changed).

## t7kb

- **The `.map` text model:** parse and print Radiant's `iwmap 4` text (entities, brushes, `mesh`/`curve` patches, layers). Oracle: every `.map` in the install round-trips byte-identical (1,561 files, 434 with patches); fuzzed. Package per the repo rule (`internal/format/` if more than one domain uses it).
- **The pipe client:** pure Go (`x/sys/windows`), tested against a fake server.
- **MCP tools**, each with its CLI twin:
  - `radiant_open`: start Radiant on a map (or reload it) and wait for the pipe; refuses to drop unsaved changes unless asked.
  - `map_find`: filtered inside Radiant (class, key, near a point, in the selection), short ids, no brush faces by default.
  - `map_edit`: ops by intent, a batch is one undo step, the reply carries the created ids and Radiant's read-back; refuses an edit whose target changed since it was read.
  - `map_view`: frame a target, capture the 3D or top view, small by default.
  - `map_command`: select, then run a Radiant command.
- The user's selection is saved and restored around every agent edit.
- **`t7kb:mapping` skill:** grid, player-scale metrics (from the knowledge base), sealing, which Radiant command does which job.
- Token report entries for the new tools.

## Done when

From a one-paragraph brief, the agent blocks out 2–3 rooms and a corridor, with a sky, a player spawn, a `volume_sun`, a few lights and a probe; the map compiles without a leak and runs in the game; the user only walked through it and commented. The run's token cost is recorded.

## What failed, or what was missing

Each Claude Code session runs its own `t7kb mcp`, and each one held about 1.2 GB of RAM from the moment it started until the session closed. That happened even in a session that never touched BO3: with two sessions open, 2.4 GB of memory sat unused. The 1.2 GB is three things loaded at start: the search vectors (~650 MB), the GDT caches (~250 MB) and the embedding model (~200 MB).

## The change

The server now starts at about 20 MB. Each part loads on the first call that needs it: the vectors and the model on the first search, the GDT caches on the first call that reads GDTs. After 10 minutes with no tool call, the server gives all three back to Windows, and the next call loads what it needs again. The cost is a slower first call: about 2.5–3 s for a search, 0.5 s for a GDT lookup. `T7KB_RELEASE_AFTER` changes the 10 minutes (`off` keeps everything loaded).

## How it was verified

- The installed 4.0.1 and this branch's binary, each driven over stdio with the real `t7kb.db`, model and BO3 install, through one session: start, two searches, a `gdt_find`, idle, then another search. The release wait was 30 s (`T7KB_RELEASE_AFTER`). Private memory:

  | | 4.0.1 | this branch |
  |---|---|---|
  | started, no call | 1191 MB | 20 MB |
  | after a search and a `gdt_find` | 1306 MB | 1332 MB |
  | idle | 1303 MB | 67 MB |
  | first search | 1.07 s | 2.95 s |
  | next search | 0.37 s | 0.18 s |
  | first `gdt_find` | 27 ms | 541 ms |
  | search after the idle release | 0.26 s | 2.5 s |

- In a real Claude Code session, with this branch's server registered for that session only and the installed plugin switched off: the server started at 20 MB, reached 1096 MB after the agent's first search, and dropped to 36 MB after 10 idle minutes. A second round went from 1128 MB down to 64 MB. The search after each release loaded everything again.
- Tests, all running in CI without the model or the BO3 install:
  - the index loads on the first search, is dropped by a release and loads again with the same ranking (`TestReleasedVectorsLoadAgainOnTheNextSearch`, plus `TestVectorIndexMatchesScan`, unchanged);
  - the embedder loads once when 8 calls race, and again after a release; `New` still fails at once without a model (`internal/embed/embed_test.go`, with a fake loader);
  - the release waits for an idle server, counts every tool call and runs until stopped (`mcp_idle_test.go`);
  - `releaseLoaded` drops the vectors and the workspaces, and the next call loads them again.
- With the real model: `TestHybridSearch` passes, and loading the model still takes 0.11 s.
- Mutation run on the first push: 14 mutants killed, 3 survived. One was a zero `T7KB_RELEASE_AFTER` (`0s` fell back to the 10-minute default while `0` meant off); the other two were the idle check's pace. The second commit makes any zero duration mean off and pins the pace (`TestIdleCheckPace`). All three now fail a test, checked by applying each one by hand. Not covered in CI: `runMCP`'s start and go-sentex's real loader, which need the database and the model.
- Ranking: unchanged. The vectors and the scoring are the same, only when they load changes, so `TestRetrievalQuality` wasn't rerun.

## Checklist

- [x] Tested live on what it drives (Radiant, the game, the mod tools), not only on fakes — the real server, database, model and BO3 install, over stdio, then in a real Claude Code session
- [x] Each `feat`, `fix` and `docs(skills)` commit subject reads as a release-note line for a modder
- [x] A changed tool: its MCP description, the skill that owns its workflow and its `docs/cli/` page updated here — no tool's surface changed; `setup-or-update`'s memory note and `docs/benchmarks.md` updated
- [x] A changed skill description: a trigger case in `plugin/evals/` added or adjusted — n/a
- [x] A skill added, renamed or removed: `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`'s description updated — n/a
- [x] No personal paths, private map content or credentials in the diff
- [x] `plugin/.claude-plugin/plugin.json`'s version left alone, unless this is the release PR

candidates.body:
Part 2 of #101, stacked on #107 (← #97).

## What changes for the agent

`build` no longer holds the call for the whole build (minutes for a link, up to half an hour for compile + light, at the risk of a client timeout). By default it **starts the build in a detached t7kb process and answers at once** with the stages it runs:

```json
{"started": "zm_x (usermap)", "pid": 27660, "stages": ["link"], "next": "the build runs on its own: …"}
```

- **`status`** (`--status`) reads how far it got: the stages planned, the one running, done, lost, and the report of the stages ended (the whole report once done).
- **`wait`** (`--wait`) runs it in the call and answers its report, as before.
- **One build of a target at a time**: a second `build` of it is refused (`a build of zm_x runs already (pid …, started 13:12, at link)`) until the first is done or lost.
- **`t7kb watch` says each build t7kb ran once, as it ends**: `build of zm_x finished ok in 12m3s: gdt, compile, light, link` (with what its link warned of and went on without), `build of zm_x failed at link after 2s: <its first errors>`, or `build of zm_x stopped at light: its process ended before the build did`. The link records of a build t7kb ran are left to that line; a Launcher link keeps its own (#107).

The CLI follows the same default (`--wait` for a terminal), as both surfaces go through one operation (`internal/cli/build_ops.go`).

## How

- **A state file per install and target** (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\t7kb\builds\<kind>-<name>-<install hash>.json`), rewritten whole at each stage (temp + rename, retried while a reader holds it). It is shared by three processes that share no memory: the build's, the MCP server answering `status`, and the watch. It outlives the build, so the verdict stays readable, and it is the lock. `Start` writes it as starting (pid 0) and the spawned process writes its own pid at once. A state whose process ended, or that has no pid after 30 s, is lost and frees its target. The rules are in `internal/build/doc.go`, under "In the background".
- **The detached process** is `t7kb build --resume <state>` (a hidden flag), started with `CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP | CREATE_NO_WINDOW`. With `DETACHED_PROCESS` it had no console, and Windows opened a visible console window for each linker run; the maintainer saw them during my test.
- **The pipeline** runs from `planned()`, the stages it will run in order, so the state can name the running stage. `gdtStage` and `planned` share `runsGDT`.

## Verified on the install

With `t7kb watch` running, on a scratch usermap, `--stages link --skip-gdt` (no gdtdb, so nothing outside the usermap is written):

| Run | Result |
| --- | --- |
| a zone with a missing xmodel | `build` returned in 47 ms (pid 27660); a second `build` was refused; `--status` said `running: link`, then `done` with the linker's error; the watch said `build of zm_t7kb_watchtest failed at link after 2s: ERROR: xmodel 't7kb_no_such_model' is missing (…)` |
| an empty zone | `build of zm_t7kb_watchtest finished ok in 2s: link` |
| a hand-run `linker_modtools` after it | `link of usermaps/zm_t7kb_watchtest ok` (the Launcher's path) |
| a build after the `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` fix | no new visible window during the link (top-level windows diffed every 100 ms) |

The scratch usermap and the state files were removed afterwards, and the install's `git status` is unchanged.

## Tests

- `internal/build`:
  - `Start` claims the target and spawns its build;
  - a second start or a waited build of the same target is refused;
  - a failed spawn leaves no state;
  - `Resume` names each stage while it runs and ends with the report;
  - a build that can't start ends its state with why;
  - lost builds (process ended, never started) free their target;
  - `Status` errors;
  - `statePath` gives one file per install and target, whatever the case;
  - `alive` on a running and an ended process;
  - the watch's build lines (ok with warnings and missing, failed, stopped, said once, not before the watch), and a t7kb build's link left to its line.
- `internal/cli`: both surfaces route start / `wait` / `status` / `--resume`; a refused start is a tool error; `spawnBuild` really starts a detached process. That process is the test binary, which `TestMain` ends at once: without that guard, each spawned copy re-ran every test and spawned again.

`CLAUDE.md` is now at 3,500 of its 3,500 words: the next addition there needs a block moved out.

| Where | Mutant | Test |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `level/brush.go:109` | a patch's lightmap coordinates `2*r+1`, `2*c+1` → `-1` | `TestAPatchIsItsControlPoints` (lightmap coordinates) |
| `level/brush.go:143` | a curve's odd column count unchecked | `TestPatchRefusals` (3 rows of 4) |
| `level/brush.go:209, 226, 249` (×2) | a 4-face or 4-corner brush refused | `TestATetrahedronIsTheLeastBrush` |

| `level/texture.go:183, 185` | an x or y wall's texture axis flipped | `TestASideWallsTilesStartOnTheOrigin` |
| `level/view.go:326` | hiding the sky breaks | `TestHidingTheSkyNamesItsBrushes` |
| `level/rev.go:29` | blank lines change a rev | `TestARevSkipsBlankLinesAndComments` |
| `level/view.go:512` | the bake's warnings capped one too early | `TestViewReportsWhatTheBakeWarnedOf` |
| `level/camera/camera.go:129` (×2) | the 2D zoom sizes a box by where it is | `TestZoomStepsCountABoxsSizeNotItsPlace` |
| `level/picture/picture.go:45, 47` (×4) | Shrink's one-pixel guard along a side that grows | `TestShrinkMeansThePixelsUnderEach` |
| `build/compilelog.go:72` | cod2map's placed problems capped one too early | `TestACompilesVerdictIsWhatCod2mapLogged` |
| `gdt/tiling.go:86` | a mipBase of `1/0` divides by zero | `TestMaterialTilingIsItsTilingOrItsLargestImage` |

## Equivalent: nothing observable changes

- **Float comparisons at a boundary the values never sit on.** These are tolerances (`< Eps`, `< 1e-6`, `< 1e-9`), a box's distance (`d > 0` adds 0 either way), the lens's checks and the 2D frame's fit:
  - `level/brush.go:260, 263, 268, 277`
  - `level/geom/geom.go:73, 153, 167`
  - `level/camera/camera.go:43, 59, 62, 65, 153`
  - `level/plan.go:244`
  - `level/texture.go:209`
  - `level/view.go:432`
- **`level/camera/camera.go:90` (×2, `-z` → `+z`).** A box is symmetric about its centre: each corner's opposite has the same `|x|`, `|y|` and the opposite `z`, so the largest distance over all corners is the same.
- **Loop bounds in the hull's and the vertices' triple loops** (`level/brush.go:240, 241`, `level/geom/geom.go:137, 138`). An extra `j` has no `k` to pair with, and starting `k` at `j-1` revisits triples whose planes are already kept.
- **Sort comparators, `<` → `<=`** (`cli/map_find.go:106`, `level/plan.go:156`, `level/view.go:255, 258`). They only reorder ties.
- **Caps where the value at exactly the cap gives the same result** (`level/view.go:256`, `level/view2d.go:167`). Slicing to the cap at the cap changes nothing.
- **`level/view2d.go:109`.** Zero zoom steps out is zero steps in.
- **`level/picture/picture.go:27, 30`.** An image exactly at the size, or square, gets the same size from either branch.
- **`level/texture.go:113`.** `rewrite` meets as many face lines as `Faces()` parsed.
- **`level/texture.go:174`.** The dominant axis of a normal is never 0.
- **`level/texture.go:206`.** An offset of 0 wraps to the size, then back to 0.
- **`level/view.go:281`.** A capture's pixels are whole RGBA quads, so `i+3` never equals the length.
- **`level/find.go:145`.** A brush of faces always has at least one.
- **`level/write.go:189`.** A patch's closing brace is its last line.
- **`level/write.go:219`.** Radiant writes no vertex with fewer than 5 fields.
- **`level/tiles.go:74`.** The scanner's starting buffer only grows.
- **`gdt/tiling.go:140`.** A tiling of 0 returns 0 either way.

## What failed, or what was missing

A Launcher compile that stopped partway (canceled, crashed or a fatal error) said nothing, or only the `.errlog` problems it got to write. Nothing told the agent the compile hadn't finished.

## The change

A compile writes its `.errlog` and `.lin` first and its `.d3dbsp` last. So when a compile's `.d3dbsp` is older than the records it wrote, it stopped before it finished. The watch now says "compile of map_source/zm/<map>.map stopped before it finished …", says where the error went (the Launcher's console, or a recompile with `build`), and adds those records.

A compile t7kb ran is left to its build's own line. A compile that stops before writing any record, as on a clean map, still says nothing. Following cod2map's process to catch that rare case was tried, then dropped as too much machinery for it.

Stacked on #148, which this branch is based on.

## How it was verified

- **Recording of real Launcher compiles of `zm_test`** (every file change under the BO3 folder, plus the mod tools' processes):
  - A full compile wrote its `.d3dbsp` last, 27 s after its `.errlog`.
  - An ents-only compile wrote it last too, 1.5 s after its `.errlog`.
  - One killed after 7 s left the previous `.d3dbsp` in place.
  - A leak doesn't stop a compile: the `.lin` is written and the `.d3dbsp` still follows.
- **Live, in a Claude Code session opened in the BO3 folder and running this version's binary** (`T7KB_BIN`):
  - A full `zm_test` compile that went to the end got the usual line (the leak, 45 problems) and no "stopped".
  - A `zm_test` compile canceled from the Launcher got "compile of map_source/zm/zm_test.map stopped before it finished …", a few seconds after the cancel, once its records had settled.
  - Two links canceled in the same session got #148's "stopped" line.
  - A canceled Light stage said nothing: the watch reads no record of that stage.
- **Precedent:** t7kb's own compile stage already judges a compile by the `.d3dbsp`'s time, at the same path.
- **Tests:** `TestRecordWatcherSaysACompileThatStoppedFromItsRecords` covers a stopped compile with problems and one with none placed yet, one that finished, and one t7kb ran. The first mutation run left one mutant alive (`len(parts) > 0` to `>= 0` in the stopped branch, a trailing `; `); the compile with nothing placed now fails on it, checked by applying it by hand. The older compile tests now write a `.d3dbsp` after their records, as a real finished compile does.

## Checklist

- [x] Tested live on what it drives (Radiant, the game, the mod tools), not only on fakes
- [x] Each `feat`, `fix` and `docs(skills)` commit subject reads as a release-note line for a modder
- [x] A changed tool: its MCP description, the skill that owns its workflow and its `docs/cli/` page updated here — no MCP tool changed; `t7kb watch`'s section in `docs/cli.md`, the package doc and `t7kb:compiling` updated
- [x] A changed skill description: a trigger case in `plugin/evals/` added or adjusted — n/a, only the body of `t7kb:compiling` changed
- [x] A skill added, renamed or removed: `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`'s description updated — n/a
- [x] No personal paths, private map content or credentials in the diff
- [x] `plugin/.claude-plugin/plugin.json`'s version left alone, unless this is the release PR

Closes #42. The link's verdict, errors and warnings now come from what the linker wrote, not from a list of known messages.

## What changes

- **`build` reads every errorlog the link wrote:**
  - the language-neutral pass's `all/assetinfo/<zone>.errorlog`;
  - each language's (`japanese/assetinfo/ja_<map>.errorlog`), which was never read.

  Each `^1` line is listed as an error and each `^3` line as a warning, with the unindented detail lines after it and the asset chain the linker indents under it (`xmodel:x < csv:zone_source/<map>.zone`). It also returns the linker's return codes. Exact repeats are listed once, and each list stops at 30, saying where the rest are.
- **Errors from the errorlog replace the console lines picked by keyword**, which missed some: the `error X1507: failed to open source file` detail of a shader failure.
- **A failed tool whose output matches no known error line** (a linker that crashed before writing its errorlog, cod2map, gdtdb) now returns its whole console output, then the exit status and a hint to offer `t7kb:contribute` once the cause is found, so t7kb's build learns the error (mutation: 9 of 9 killed).
- **Fixed:** a mod's zone that linked with warnings only failed the build, because the errorlog was read for usermaps only.
- **`compiling` skill:**
  - The exit-code section becomes the method: search each entry's fixed words in the knowledge base, fix it where its chain points with the skill that owns it, relink until the summary is clean. It says what `missing` means, the one entry the corpus can't explain. As decided, it gives no per-message table: the corpus already holds those fixes.
  - The publish section moves to `references/publish.md`, ahead of #39. The body goes from 2,699 words (2.8.0) to 2,419.
- **The `build` MCP description, `references/cli.md` and CLAUDE.md** say what the report holds.

## Verified

- **The reader on the install's real errorlogs:**
  - `zm_t7kb_demo`: 7 xmodel warnings, each with its chain;
  - `zm_test`: the bulletmesh warning, and an old Japanese pass's `^1 xmodel '…' is missing` errors, which `build` never reported.
- **Tests on fixtures:**
  - the CRLF format with chains, repeats and unindented detail lines;
  - an indented line before any entry, an unreadable errorlog;
  - the cap at exactly 30 and beyond, the 2 s age margin;
  - map and mod links with warnings only, a mod zone failing with two errors;
  - the printed summary.
- **Mutation testing** of the changed lines (go-mutesting, parallel clones): the first pass left 12 survivors and found the dropped detail line, now fixed and tested. The second pass kills all 67 mutants.

The agent edits the map open in the user's Radiant through the t7_radiant_bridge plugin (McReaper/t7_radiant_bridge#3).

## The probes op (2026-10-17)

- **`map_edit`'s `probes` op** probes the space players reach, on any map: from `at` (default the `info_player_start`) it walks the floor a player gets to (a step of 18 up, any drop off a ledge, a body's room and width; stairs, upper storeys and prefabs' brushes included, prefabs read from `map_source`; clips and `nonColliding` brushes passed through), keeps on a map with zones to what lies in them (out of them a player dies), and boxes it: the largest boxes first, floor to ceiling, sides snapped onto the walls' faces, none overlapping. A lintel, a storey or a stair through an opening parts boxes; a sealed space gets none (it would bake out of range). Each box is a `reflection_probe` at Treyarch's defaults (4x, AO 8, blend 3), its blend longer over floor no box holds. `replace` swaps the probes already there; `global` moves the global probe into the largest box (an `info_null` the `volume_sun` targets). Cells are sampled as the walk reaches them, so a skybox's extent costs nothing.
- **Checked offline against hand-placed probes** (a fake Radiant serving copies of the maps): on zm_floorplan it lays the boxes the scripted pass had plus the strips it missed (64 for 49); on zm_test it fills the zoned play space in about 2.5 s. zm_test's own probes set two rules: blends of 3, and drops (without them most of the map went unreached; without zones, the walk fell into the out-of-bounds terrain).
- **What it leaves to a lighter** (the lighting skill says so): walls off the axes (axis boxes leave slivers), what players see but don't stand in (vistas, rooms behind windows), floor reached only by jumping.
- **Tests:** two rooms and a door, storeys and a stair through an opening, an L-shaped room, a soffit strip and the blends on every side, corridors 48 and 40 wide on either grid line, a gap narrower than a body, ledges, zones and the cells kept past them, prefabs nested, scaled and turned, a patch floor, the capture point over a stair, the map's corners. Two fixes came from them: samples sat on the grid's 4s, where 8-thick walls put their faces (a 48-wide corridor read 40), and a roof exactly at the sky cap counted as sky.
- **Mutation pass**, by hand (a 1,347-mutant batch was too heavy for the owner's machine; 268 never ran): the survivors left change nothing observable (`dir` is always ±1, the grid's empty ring, unique group keys, boundaries at eps, the blend's 32 cap absorbing the run's, bounding-box early-outs the exact test repeats) or are tuning constants (the 16-unit ceiling step, the capture point's 16-unit nudge, five lines per side).
- **Not yet tried in Radiant.**

- Split `internal/level` (7,850 lines in one package) into packages by concern, so a mutant reruns only its own package's tests.
- `map_check`: floor in no zone, surfaces no probe covers; then a lights op; then probes, lights, fog and SSI set together.
- The blockout run (#52's step 4): from a short brief, rooms and a corridor with a sky, a spawn, a `volume_sun`, lights and probes; compiled without a leak, played, walked through by the user; its token cost recorded.

Part 2 of the M1a stack (#52, a milestone of #51), split out of #68 so each PR's checks (coverage of changed lines, mutation) run on its own lines. Base: `feat/radiant-map-1-client` (#71). Merge bottom-up, each only with the owner's go-ahead; before merging a base with `--delete-branch`, retarget the PR above it to `main`, or GitHub closes it. Draft.

The agent edits the map open in the user's Radiant through the t7_radiant_bridge plugin (McReaper/t7_radiant_bridge#3).

## The map tools

- `map_find` / `t7kb map find` (`internal/level`): the entities of the map open in Radiant, unsaved edits included, filtered by ids, class, key, a point's neighbourhood or the user's selection, each with a short id (a GUID's first 8 hex digits, more when needed), origin or bounds, naming keys, and on request its brushes and patches. No face is shown.
  - Brush bounds come from the face planes. `TestBrushBoxesMatchRadiants` (opt-in on a test Radiant's pid) compares every brush with Radiant's own selection bounds: all 8,782 brushes and patches of the install's largest prefab agree, once two rules of Radiant's are applied (a box thinner than 0.25 is widened to 0.25; a brush whose planes enclose nothing has none). Over the install: 1,562 maps, 40,687 brushes, 27,941 patches, two empty brushes (in `zm_test`, empty for Radiant too).
- `map_view` / `t7kb map view`: an image of the 3D view or a 2D view (top, front, side), framed on ids, a point, a camera pose, or as it is, with the short ids written where they landed (and listed with their pixel positions); a shot may use another render method (fake lighting for an unbaked blockout). The MCP answer is the projection as JSON, then the PNG (768 px by default, about 400 tokens).
  - Radiant's lens was measured (a pinhole, f ≈ 1212 px for a 1648×869 view; the tests replay those projections) and a framed shot recovers it from where the target's corners landed, then keeps it per Radiant. 2D framing sets the zoom from 100% in steps of 1.25, then centres through the camera.
  - Two traps the live runs found: zooming moves the 2D view's centre, and turning its axis centres it on the camera. So the user's view is read on the axis it shows, and put back axis, then zoom, then centre. Checked live from a turned, zoomed, off-centre 2D view: axis, scale, centre and camera all came back.

- `map_edit` / `t7kb map edit --ops`: a batch of ops (box brushes in worldspawn or as new brush entities, point entities, deletes, keys, moves, materials) applied in order and sent as the bridge's `edit` (plugin 1.1.0, McReaper/t7_radiant_bridge#3): one entry in Radiant's undo menu, whole or not at all. A point entity keeps its id; a world brush or a brush entity is rebuilt under a new one (`was` gives the old), since that is what Radiant's undo restores exactly. The answer reads the map back: each op's id, class, origin or bounds.
  - Live: eight ops showed as one "Undo t7kb: a first room", every op found back, Radiant's own bounds of the new box were the ones asked, and one Ctrl+Z gave back the map with its GUIDs, materials and keys, unmodified.
  - A live test of the plugin's rollback sent a malformed brush line on purpose: Radiant took it for a fatal error (dialogs in front of the user, the plugin disabled mid-call) rather than a refusal. The plugin now checks every text bound for Radiant's import first, and refuses what Radiant can't read.
- `map_command` / `t7kb map command`: one of Radiant's own menu entries (CSG Hollow, Subtract, Merge…) on what the ids name, selected alone, then the user's selection back; the answer gives what it created and deleted, and its undo entry; `--menu` lists a menu. Live: CSG Hollow on a new box gave six 8-unit walls under "Undo hollow", and the user's selection came back.

## The skill

`t7kb:mapping` now owns the map tools' workflow (open, find, edit in batches the user would undo whole, look top first, Radiant's own tools, save before building), and `references/map-tools.md` holds what a blockout needs: Treyarch's scale standards (`docs_modtools/Scale_Standards.pdf`), what a map from the ZM Mod Level template already holds (sky box, start zone, volumes, spawns), which edits change an id, and traps checked in a test Radiant on a copy of the template — `CSG Subtract` carves every brush its cutter touches, the start zone's and the sun's volumes included, so doors are built around the hole; `CSG Hollow`'s walls are as thick as the grid; `File/Save` saves with no dialog, and the build compiles the file, not Radiant's memory. A new trigger case passes, and the two existing mapping cases still do.

## The token report

`TestTokenReport` now measures the map tools on the stock ZM Mod Level template's map, served by the fake Radiant with the views measured on a real one, images counted as Claude prices them (width × height / 750); `docs/benchmarks.md` has the rows in a section of their own. A room costs about a thousand tokens: the ops an agent writes (254), the answer (212), a top view to check it (48 + 467). The whole map's `map_find` is the dearest call (1,598 tokens for 33 entities), so its filters matter.

## Mutation pass

The CI's `mutate` job over the branch's changed lines went from 164 lived mutants (efficacy 83.75%) to 29 (97%+). The tests that closed the gap pin: the labels' drawing (two ASCII goldens read glyph by glyph: the four places around a point, pairs one pixel either side of overlapping, points off the image), every pixel of a capture's conversion and its scaling's means, the focal from the point most off centre, a degenerate face and a cut leaning in z, short ids at the head of the sorted list, a point framed with or without its radius, the thousand label points nearest a target, a shot whose corners all fell behind, fits at its edges, batch counts that summed to zero under a mutant, an entity's two brushes moved, the 200-row cap, no negative zero.

The 29 left from the first pass change nothing observable: boundaries at 1e-6, 1e-9, eps and 0

`zone_predict` (with `internal/deps`, the dependency graph it ran on) re-implements the linker's walk of references to predict a link. Checked against the `.deps` the linker writes at every link, it reports references the linker never looks for:

What it predicted before a link, `zone_explain` and `zone_contents` read exactly from the last link's report.

Its one real finding was worth keeping: **a reference to an asset no GDT defines doesn't fail the link.** The linker links on without it and logs nothing, so a material shows without that texture in game. The `.deps` records every lookup, with an empty hash for one that found nothing.

- **`build`:** after a link, it lists those names ("linked without"), each with the asset that named it, per zone for a mod, capped at 10. Closes #47.

## What changes

- **`t7kb unpack-db`** (new, `internal/cli/db.go`), run by both installers after each download: compares `t7kb.db` with the zip's entry (size, then the CRC-32 the zip records) and unpacks only when they differ, so an update whose release carried the same database forward rewrites nothing. When a running t7kb server holds `t7kb.db` open (Windows can't replace an open file), the new database waits as `t7kb.db.new` and the command says to close every agent session.
- **`ensureDB`** swaps a staged `t7kb.db.new` in at the next start; if another t7kb still holds the db, it notes it on stderr and keeps serving the old one. It still unpacks a missing db from the zip (manual installs).
- **`install.ps1`**: moves a running `t7kb.exe` aside before extracting (Windows can rename a running exe, not overwrite it — `Expand-Archive` failed with "Access denied" from a Claude Code session, which is how the setup skill runs it) and deletes it right away when no session runs it; checks curl's exit code (PowerShell 5.1 doesn't throw on a native failure, so a failed db download still printed "t7kb installed"); downloads the zip to a `.part`; reports the staged case instead of "t7kb installed". No new `exit`: piped into `iex` it would close the user's PowerShell.
- **`install.sh`**: same download-then-move and `unpack-db` (on Linux the swap always succeeds: a running server keeps reading the old inode).
- Both installers run `unpack-db` only when `t7kb --help` lists it: they come from `main`, the binary from the latest release, and a release that predates the command would take `unpack-db` for a browse query and wait on stdin. Until the next release, they keep today's behaviour.
- Setup skill, README, CLAUDE.md and the release footer say the installer unpacks the database, and what to relay when it is staged.

## Verified

- Unit tests for every branch of `ensureDB`/`syncDB`, with a `rename` seam standing in for the Windows lock.
- Both installers run end to end against a local fake release (file:// URLs): fresh install; `-Force` while a t7kb from the target holds the exe and the db (Windows: exe moved aside, db staged, "Access is denied" reported); the swap at the next start; `-Force` with an unchanged database ("already matches", nothing rewritten). Linux under WSL, with a reader holding the db: swapped immediately. The installer with the released 2.9.0 binary skips `unpack-db` and finishes.
- Mutation testing on the changed lines: 35 mutants, 30 killed.
