The adversarial review (2026-08-08, verdict: **needs-rework**) found this issue not safe to execute as filed: its evidentiary base (`docs/plan/evidence/BRIEF.md`, `11-analog-determination.md`) does not exist on the default branch and its pinned `evidence_commit` is unreachable from `master`; three open questions marked "blocks execution" were left unresolved in a `tier: task` filing; the flagship cross-platform determinism claim (H1) was tested only manually, not by CI; the anti-cheat prediction P3 was gameable (no quantitative bound, only a prose warning); the task's own numbers admitted a 3.25× gap between its "core slice" estimate and its stated real cost; and the DoD cited an undefined external "rule" numbering with no governing document anywhere in the tree.

The visionary review (2026-08-08, verdict: **endorse-with-reframing**) accepted the underlying goal — a committable, gradeable analog answer — but argued for three changes: (1) make a residual/conservation certificate the correctness gate and demote the digest to a change tripwire, because a digest proves the bits didn't move, not that they were ever right; (2) build the determinism harness around the smallest possible kernel first, so the byte-identity claim is falsified or confirmed in days, not after the full device set lands; (3) drop sparse LU and the Markowitz tie-break, because they contradict the parent feature's own recorded deferral of sparse factorization and manufacture the exact risk the issue then names as its "least-derisked" item.

**Since both reviews were written, the parent feature #351 (FEAT-046) was independently rewritten (2026-08-10)**, on its own visionary review, redirecting to a **v1 scope**: linear devices only (R, L, C, V, I — no diode, no Newton-Raphson, no junction limiting, no escape ladder), dense LU (sparse factorization deferred, matching this issue's visionary review point for point), and a **fixed declared timestep** (no adaptive LTE step control). #351's rewrite names this issue directly: *"TASK-0097 (filed as #463)... as filed, #463 targets the full nonlinear engine... and needs re-scoping or splitting against this v1 plan."* Sibling task #397 (TASK-0100, already rewritten) has gone further and already assumes this re-scoped shape, carrying `blocked_by: [463, 481]` against "the dense-LU solver core... no Newton loop." Sibling task #402 (TASK-0099, already rewritten) has moved its controlled-source and waveform stamps out of its own scope specifically pending this task's re-scope.

This rewrite enacts the re-scope together with both reviews' fixes: **this issue is now FEAT-046 v1's dense-LU linear solver core** — R/L/C/V/I stamps only, one totally-ordered pivot tie-break with no Markowitz term, one LU factorization per fixture (the matrix is constant by construction once every device is linear and the step is fixed), trapezoidal integration at a fixed declared step, and a **residual/conservation certificate as the correctness gate**, with the digest demoted to a determinism tripwire owned jointly with TASK-0098 (#481). The nonlinear engine — Newton-Raphson, junction limiting, the escape ladder, adaptive LTE control, the diode stamp — moves to **FEAT-046b, not filed**, per #351's own disposition; this rewrite does not build it and does not file a new issue for it.

Everything below states this issue's current, narrowed intent. It does not narrate how the issue got here, and no comment on this thread needs to be read to understand it.

**This issue may not be treated as ready to land** until the governance gap #351 and #402 both name is closed: `docs/capability-roadmap/README.md` section 6(a) ("What still stays out" → "Different tool class") currently places continuous-time/analog work outside JLS's tool class — "a different tool, not a deeper digital model", at `docs/capability-roadmap/README.md:1041` as read at `828822672f`. The second sentence previously quoted here, "No continuous-time solver, and none should be added", is **not in that file**: it is `docs/capability-roadmap/sweep-06-physical-boundary.md:83`, written inside that document's IBIS/Touchstone row rather than as a programme-wide prohibition. Nothing in `ARCHITECTURE.md`'s "Recorded decisions" reverses either. Both roadmap documents were deleted from the default branch in `4882e93`, after this issue was pinned; they still resolve at `828822672f`, and `ARCHITECTURE.md` still exists at HEAD. This issue restates the gate; it does not close it.

## Abstract

`jls -b` today prints results to stdout and (optionally) a VCD file, but never writes anything a second, independent process can look up later: there is no committed, self-describing record of *which* circuit, `-t` vectors, `-s` params and `-d` limit produced a given run's outcome. That gap blocks #679 (the pure aggregator) and #369 (the grading harness), both of which need a per-job artifact to fold or consume, and it blocks any campaign tooling from telling "this job's output" apart from "this job never ran." The remedy is a receipt: a deterministic, digest-named, line-oriented text record — carrying input digests, JLS version, the existing §3 watched-output block, and exit status, and nothing that varies by clock, host, pid, thread, or worker — written by `jls -b` itself, with a malformed or unreadable input refused through the existing `jls.LoadError` taxonomy rather than defaulted or silently repaired.

## Intended Audience & Impact

- **Instructors authoring, grading, or auto-checking work in batch (`-b`) mode**, and anyone running a multi-run campaign (#350's scope): today there is nothing to `diff`, archive, or hand to a grading script after a batch run except stdout text captured ad hoc by the invoking shell. A receipt gives them a durable, reviewable artifact per job, named so that re-running the same job never silently overwrites or duplicates it under a different name.
- **Contributors and maintainers building #679 (the aggregator) and #369 (the grading harness)**: both are specified as *consumers* of this task's format rather than inventors of their own (#350 "Resolved design decisions" item 1, and #350's own Scope item 2 quoted in §1 below). Without this task landing first, neither has a format to build against — confirmed structurally: `git grep -ni "receipt"` across `*.java` and `*.md` at the evidence commit finds no receipt writer or format anywhere in the tree outside unrelated collaborative-editing code (`src/jls/collab/session/Roster.java`, `docs/collaborative-editing-research.md`), i.e. the capability does not exist yet (§2 O1).
- **LLM agents and future executors of #679**: AC4 requires a single named, reusable digest function so the aggregator's own collision check calls it instead of re-deriving the digest — this task is the one place that function is allowed to be defined.

## Status & Dependencies

```yaml
tier: task
evidence_commit: c5cee1baff3451a85787b4a09bd0b2b05af7dfdd
owned_by_derived: [350]  # DERIVED from feature rosters, NOT authoritative;
                        #   the owning features' requires_tasks are the only record.
                        #   Regenerate rather than hand-edit (validator G21).
blocked_by: []         # foundational: translated from the pre-migration `ordering_after: []`
                        #   — no other task or feature must land before this one
blocks: [679]           # TASK-C350-4 (the aggregator): #679's own body lists
                        #   "TASK-C350-1" (this task) in its ordering_after, and its AC
                        #   requires calling this task's digest function (AC4) rather
                        #   than reimplementing it
related: [369]          # FEAT-053 (grading harness): consumes this task's receipt
                        #   vocabulary as its per-item result record (#350 "Resolved
                        #   design decisions" item 1) — reference only, not blocking
# pre-migration compact-form fields, carried forward per migration instructions:
#   task_id (banned form): TASK-C350-1
#   band_mw (banned form): 0.5-1 maintainer-weeks (#350 "Cost": "receipt format (~0.5-1 mw)")
```

## 1. Background & Prior Work

This task is the first of two tasks #350 (FEAT-057, "many independent runs dispatch across cores or hosts and aggregate into one report whose contents do not depend on how many workers ran") requires; its `requires_tasks` field lists exactly `[674, 679]` (`gh issue view 350`, Status & Dependency Graph block, observed 2026-08-18). #350's own scope statement for this piece:

> "Each `jls -b` run emits a self-describing, deterministic **receipt**: digests of the circuit file, the `-t` vectors, the `-s` params, the `-d` limit, the JLS version, and the §3 watched-output block, plus exit status. No clock, host, pid, or worker id appears in a receipt." (#350, Capability Statement & Scope Boundary, item 2)

and its path/fold math, which this task's AC4 digest function must satisfy:

> "$\mathrm{path}(j) = \mathrm{digest}(\mathrm{inputs}(j))$, digest injective on $J$ ... so a name collision is a rejected job list at read time, not a lost or overwritten artifact." (#350, "Transformations at the feature boundary")

Prior art already in the tree that this task should reuse rather than reinvent:

- **Content-addressed digesting.** `Circuit.java` already has a public SHA-256-hex digest of a circuit's canonical form:

  > "A hash of this circuit's canonical serialized form (#166): equal for any two circuits with identical content, whatever their load/edit history." — [`Circuit.java` L1539-L1541](https://github.com/anadon/JLS/blob/c5cee1baff3451a85787b4a09bd0b2b05af7dfdd/src/jls/Circuit.java#L1539-L1541)

  `stateHash()`'s body ([L1548-L1568](https://github.com/anadon/JLS/blob/c5cee1baff3451a85787b4a09bd0b2b05af7dfdd/src/jls/Circuit.java#L1548-L1568)) is `MessageDigest.getInstance("SHA-256")` over UTF-8 bytes, rendered as lower-case hex — the exact shape AC4's digest function needs for each declared input, and for `path(job)` itself.
- **Structured, categorized load failures.** `src/jls/LoadError.java` is a record — `category`, `detail`, `line`, `element`, `hint` — [L31-L32](https://github.com/anadon/JLS/blob/c5cee1baff3451a85787b4a09bd0b2b05af7dfdd/src/jls/LoadError.java#L31-L32) — with a fixed `Category` enum (`IO_ERROR`, `NOT_A_CIRCUIT`, `MALFORMED`, `NEWER_FORMAT`, `UNKNOWN_ELEMENT`, `ELEMENT_ERROR`, `LIMIT_EXCEEDED`, [L41-L66](https://github.com/anadon/JLS/blob/c5cee1baff3451a85787b4a09bd0b2b05

## Abstract

A push to a first-time contributor's own fork of JLS produces **no Actions run at all** in that fork — not a run "waiting on maintainer approval," but zero runs, because both `ci.yml` and `codeql.yml` restrict their `push` trigger to `branches: ["master"]`, a branch a fork's feature branch never is. This leaves contributors with no fast, independent pass/fail signal before opening a PR. The remedy is one new, small workflow — a single `contributor-check` job running `mvn -B verify` (compile + headless tests + SpotBugs + NullAway, the same thresholds `build` already enforces) — added as its own workflow file so the existing 14-job `ci.yml` fleet's triggers, cost profile, and #47 double-build guard are untouched.

## Intended Audience & Impact

- **Contributors, especially first-time ones**, who today get silence from their fork's Actions tab on every push and only find out whether their change compiles, passes tests, or trips SpotBugs/NullAway once they open a PR against upstream (at which point the "Require approval for first-time contributors" Actions setting may additionally delay even that signal behind a maintainer click — a separate, not-yet-built control tracked on #568). After this task, the same contributor gets a fork-local, self-service verdict on every push, before a PR exists.
- **Maintainers**, who are not asked to do anything to produce this verdict: `contributor-check` runs entirely inside the fork's own Actions context, with `contents: read` only and zero `secrets.*` references, so it costs the upstream repository nothing and exposes no upstream secret to a fork's workflow run.

## Status & Dependencies

```yaml
tier: task
evidence_commit: c5cee1baff3451a85787b4a09bd0b2b05af7dfdd
owned_by_derived: [568]  # DERIVED from feature rosters, NOT authoritative;
                        #   the owning features' requires_tasks are the only record.
                        #   Regenerate rather than hand-edit (validator G21).
blocked_by: []
blocks: []
related: []
```

Sequencing note carried from the prior body (not encoded as a graph edge — see §11 (Threats to Validity) and Open Questions): this task's contributor-facing benefit is not independently evidenced against #514's actual bounced-PR causes (#4/#5, #187), which trace to review latency and `SimpleEditor`'s size, not CI feedback time. Worth doing regardless, but should not be sequenced as though it fixes #514.

## 1. Background & Prior Work

`ci.yml`'s `push` trigger was deliberately narrowed to `branches: ["master"]` by issue #47, so that a branch with an open PR builds once (via `pull_request`) rather than twice (once via `push`, once via `pull_request`):

```
3:# push is limited to master so a branch with an open PR builds once,
4:# not twice (issue #47); the nightly cron runs ONLY the gui-wayland lane
```
(`.github/workflows/ci.yml:3-4` at c5cee1b)

`codeql.yml` carries the identical restriction, added for issue #67 (CodeQL static analysis on push/PR/weekly):

```
3:# Static analysis for security issues on every push/PR and weekly
4:# (issue #67). Alerts appear under the repository's Security tab.
```
(`.github/workflows/codeql.yml:3-4 (quotes: `# (issue #67). Alerts appear under the repository's Security tab.`)` at c5cee1b)

The `contents: read` least-privilege posture that `contributor-check` must inherit was established repo-wide by issue #68:

```
15:# least-privilege token: the build only reads the repo (issue #68)
16:permissions:
17:  contents: read
```
(`.github/workflows/ci.yml:15-17` at c5cee1b)

The thresholds `contributor-check` must match — SpotBugs threshold High and NullAway as a compile-time error — were established by issues #54 and #93 respectively (see §2 (Observations), items 5-6).

## 2. Observations

1. `ci.yml`'s push trigger matches only `master`:
   ```
   8:on:
   9:  push:
   10:    branches: ["master"]
   11:  pull_request:
   ```
   (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:8-11` at c5cee1b)

2. `codeql.yml`'s push trigger is identical:
   ```
   6:on:
   7:  push:
   8:    branches: ["master"]
   9:  pull_request:
   ```
   (`.github/workflows/codeql.yml:6-9` at c5cee1b)

3. No third workflow file exists at c5cee1b that could catch a fork push on a non-master branch. Command run: `git ls-tree -r --name-only c5cee1baff3451a85787b4a09bd0b2b05af7dfdd -- .github/workflows/`. Output:
   ```
   .github/workflows/ci.yml
   .github/workflows/codeql.yml
   .github/workflows/mutation.yml
   .github/workflows/release.yml
   .github/workflows/repro-installers.yml
   .github/workflows/scorecard.yml
   ```
   None is named `contributor-check.yml`, and none of the six declares an unrestricted `push` trigger (each was checked individually; four of the six declare a `push` key and every one of them is narrowed: `ci.yml` and `codeql.yml` to `branches: ["master"]` (Observations 1-2), `scorecard.yml` likewise to `branches: ["master"]` (`.github/workflows/scorecard.yml:10-11` at c5cee1b), and `release.yml` to `tags: ["v*"]` (`.github/workflows/release.yml:21-22` at c5cee1b); only `repro-installers.yml` and `mutation.yml` declare no `push` trigger at all, carrying `schedule`/`workflow_dispatch` alone). **This is the observed failure**: at c5cee1b, a push to any non-master branch of a fork produces zero workflow runs, by construction of the trigger filters in Observations 1-2 combined with the absence of any broader-triggered workflow in Observation 3. Per the maintainer's improvement-evidence ruling, this structural absence (verified read-only via `git ls-tree` and the trigger blocks quoted above) stands in for a build-observed failure — there is no `mvn` command whose failure would demonstrate "a workflow did not start."

4. `ci.yml` defines 14 top-level jobs at c5cee1b (not the 15 the prior body's AC-1 stated — see Open Questions). Command: `awk '/^jobs:/{f=1} f && /^  [a-zA-Z0-9_-]+:$/{print}' ci.yml` against the file at c5cee1b. Output, in order: `build` (ci.yml:28), `windows` (ci.yml:143), `macos` (ci.yml:259), `

## Abstract

JLS has no committed, reproducible benchmark instrument for the simulation event loop. The only throughput figures currently published — `docs/capability-roadmap/keystone-c-performance.md`'s "≈ 8,090 simulated CPU cycles per second" warm-loop figure and its "≈ 1,100–1,450 cycles/s" CLI-inclusive figure — were produced by scratch harness files under a session-local `/tmp` path that are not in the tree, and `riscv/bench_kernel.py` only ever timed one subprocess `java -jar` call end to end (JVM boot, load, and simulation folded together), which is too noisy to serve as a per-fixture measurement. This task adds a production batch-mode flag to `JLSStart`'s `FLAGS` table — driving the existing `beforeEvent()`/`afterEvent()` hooks via a `Simulator` subclass — plus a single documented `-Pbench`, `@Tag("bench")` surefire execution that loops that flag over the fixture set, so any party who checks out the tree can reproduce per-fixture `ns/event`, `events/cycle`, the `initSimulation`/`runEventLoop` phase split, the full event census, and the node-count/element-mix census with one command, with each figure's clocking regime derived by observation rather than hand-typed.

## Intended Audience & Impact

**Contributors and maintainers doing sim event-loop performance work.** #442's band/event-count gate, #476's queue-share investigation, #393's queue-traffic reduction work, and #879's k2000 loop-time gate each need a comparable, reproducible measurement of the same event loop; without a shared instrument, each would hand-roll its own probe and produce numbers that cannot be checked against one another or against this task's own output. This task is the single instrument all four (plus #735's ratio-gate lane, per #557's structural review) read from.

**External reviewers and anyone who cites the published performance figures.** `docs/capability-roadmap/keystone-c-performance.md` publishes cycles/s and ns/event figures today (Observation O2 below) with no committed instrument behind them — its own "Reproduction" section names a session-scratch `/tmp` path and files that were never committed (Observation O3). After this task, the class of figure that document headlines has a documented, in-tree, single-command reproduction path.

## Status & Dependencies

                        #   Regenerate rather than hand-edit (validator G21).

  - 413   # a meaningful CPU-scale throughput figure needs #413's re-homed anchor;
          # Observation O9 lists the four entries tracked under test/fixtures/
          # today and establishes none of them as a CPU-scale design — the
          # harness itself is NOT blocked, only CPU-scale calibration/reporting is
          # (see § Boundary carried into §12/§13 below)
blocks: []
related:
  - 393   # #393: queue-traffic reduction reads this instrument's event census
  - 442   # #442 TASK-0026: owns the band gate and the committed event-census golden;
          #   its §7.5 refusal to promote a counting subclass into src/ governs its
          #   own test-only census producer, not this one
  - 476   # #476: queue-share work reads this instrument
  - 557   # #557: structural review that assigned this issue as #735's entry point
  - 728   # TASK-C554-2: widens the fixture population this harness loops over
  - 730   # TASK-C554-3: owns the machine-readable run-record schema this harness's

  - 732   # doc that explains the startup gap in prose instead of citing a stored

  - 735   # TASK-C557-1: calls this harness's comparison-mode entry point instead of
          #   reimplementing ratio evaluation
  - 879   # #879: k2000 loop-time gate reads this instrument

## Proposed disposition

A visionary-lens review (2026-08-08, verdict: endorse-with-reframing) endorsed this task's
core claim — JLS needs one addressing key that names an element inside a nested instance, a net,
and a fused net group — but argued the route was wrong on four points: (1) the `view` field
does not belong in the key at all, since a view is a property of a placement table, not of the
addressed subject; (2) net identity should be **derived** from content rather than **minted and
persisted**, because the hard case — merge and split — cannot be answered by a minted id either,
and a derived id removes the format change, the golden regeneration, the legacy-minting pass, and
the dependency on `ElementId.parse`'s counter guard entirely; (3) group identity's existing
derivation (H5, unchanged by the review) should not be the odd one out — nets should be derived
the same way, which resolves the asymmetry a companion adversarial review separately flagged; and
(4) the task bundles a free half (the address type, `Ops.resolve` descent, the uniqueness-check
move — no format change, no blocker) with an expensive, contested half (persisted net identity)
and should be organized around that cost seam. A companion adversarial-lens review (2026-08-08,
verdict: needs-rework) independently verified that the persisted-net-id design's own cited
justification was false on `master` (O5 quoted a counter-advance guard in `ElementId.parse` that
does not exist there — it is issue #491's *proposed*, unlanded fix), that the resulting dependency
on #491 was undeclared, that the net/group asymmetry above was a real durability hazard, and that
the format-epoch coordination the issue called a "real cost" was not enforced anywhere.

**Since both reviews, the owning feature (#318, FEAT-014) has itself been rewritten** and has
independently converged on exactly the visionary review's direction: content-derived net and
group identity (no new persisted field, no format bump, no legacy-minting story) plus a derived,
non-persisted instance-path type — and it says so explicitly: *"#472 (TASK-0035) ... specifies a
minted, persisted `ItemKey`/`nid` scheme ... the mechanism this issue no longer asks for ... A
maintainer needs to re-scope, redirect, or close #472."* This rewrite performs that reconciliation
directly on #472 rather than filing new issues: it keeps the TASK-0035 designator, narrows and
restructures the scope to `#318`'s current TASK-A ("content-derived net and group identity,
over the single partition #468 provides") and TASK-B ("a derived, non-persisted instance-path
value type in `jls.core`"), and organizes the Method section around the cost seam the visionary
review identified — an address-type-and-resolution part with no blocker, and a net/group-identity
part blocked on #468. This issue is not closed, merged, or split into new issues by this rewrite.

The reframing dissolves the adversarial review's findings by construction rather than by patching
them: there is no `ElementId.parse` counter guard to depend on (finding 1) or omit from
`blocked_by` (finding 2), because nothing is minted; there is no format epoch to coordinate with
#436/#437 (finding 3), because nothing is persisted; the net/group asymmetry (finding 6) is gone,
because both are now derived the same way; and the completion criteria below replace
self-attested "spot-check" language (finding 4) with assertions a test can fail. The bundling
finding (finding 5) is addressed by the two-part Method structure below rather than by filing
separate issues.

### Unabsorbed review findings (recorded 2026-08-16)

The 2026-08-08 dual-lens review raised the following points that this body neither adopts nor explicitly declines. Recorded pending maintainer disposition; recording is not endorsement.

- Visionary review, §4 ("The identity that is actually broken today"): `Wire.save` is a no-op and `WireEnd.init` rebuilds each `Wire` with a fresh `sid` on every load, so `AttachProbe`'s existing sid-based binding already breaks across save/load — the reviewer called this "the strongest argument for the reframing" and recommended a one-line fix in `WireEnd.save`. The rewritten body adopts the reframing's conclusion (derived, non-persisted net/group identity) but does not mention this wire-sid durability bug or the recommended `WireEnd.save` fix anywhere — not in O2 (which only restates "Wire.save is a no-op" as a convenience for derivation, not as a pre-existing probe-binding defect), not in Related Work, not in Open Questions, not in scope/out-of-scope.

## Abstract

JLS can address an element (`sid`) and nothing else. Nets have no identity at all, fused net
groups have none, and there is no way to name an element *inside a particular subcircuit
instance* — the invariant `sid` is unique per `CIRCUIT` block holds today only because
`SubCircuit.save` inlines a full copy of the definition per instance, which is exactly what
shared definitions (#447) will remove. This task specifies and implements `jls.core.ItemKey`, a
`(instancePath, sid)` address with **no view component and no persisted form**; content-derived
identity for a net (the least member wire-end `sid`, under the existing canonical order) and for
a jump-fused group (the least member net id); and moves the load-time uniqueness check to
`(instancePath, sid)` — the invariant that survives sharing. Nothing here is written to any
`.jls` file: every existing file, and the full golden corpus, stays byte-identical.

## Intended Audience & Impact

- **Circuit-file authors and third-party tools that read or write `.jls` files** — unaffected.
  No new attribute, no grammar change to the file format, no `FORMAT` bump. `ItemKey` and
  derived net/group identity are in-memory computations only.
- **Students drawing and simulating circuits** — protected: nothing about how a file loads or
  saves changes, so nothing they have drawn changes meaning or changes bytes on disk. Served

## Abstract

`BootListenerHygieneTest.assertNoNewListeners` — the precise half of the runtime pin for issue #168's prediction P3 ("no headless boot path opens a network listener") — gates its only exact assertion on `/proc/self/net/tcp`/`tcp6` through `assumeTrue`, so on macOS (which has no `/proc`) that assertion never executes: both of the class's `@Test` methods abort at the `assertNoNewListeners` call, which JUnit reports as *aborted* and Maven Surefire counts as *skipped* rather than passed, leaving the coarse `assertTimeoutPreemptively` pin and the boot-path sanity assertions that ran before it as the only checks that execute. Sibling issue #665 has separately been rewritten to give the two other `/proc`-gated test files a portable, unconditional observation, but its scope explicitly does not reach this third probe. This task gives `assertNoNewListeners` the same treatment — a portable macOS-safe observation if one can be built without a subprocess tool, or, failing that, a narrow, evidence-backed, single-method documented skip — so the invariant it backs is either actually checked on macOS or its remaining gap is stated plainly rather than silently rotting.

## Intended Audience & Impact

- **Contributors, maintainers, and LLM agents working the codebase.** Today, `mvn verify` on a macOS checkout (and the advisory `macos` CI lane, [`ci.yml#L259-L263`](https://github.com/anadon/JLS/blob/c5cee1baff3451a85787b4a09bd0b2b05af7dfdd/.github/workflows/ci.yml#L259-L263)) reports `batchModeOpensNoListener` and `defaultGuiStartOpensNoListener` as *skipped* — JUnit aborts them (O1) rather than passing them, and the build stays green either way — while the one assertion that precisely checks "no new LISTEN socket" never runs; only the coarser `assertTimeoutPreemptively` pin does. Landing this task lets a maintainer close out #265 Stage 8 and #665's cross-reference to this issue with an actual disposition instead of an open gap.

## Proposed disposition

Neither review recommends closing, merging, or splitting this issue. The adversarial review
(verdict: needs-rework) found the issue unstartable as filed: its governing citation —
`docs/parity-contract.md`, quoted at length and captioned "do not restate it; implement it" — has
never existed on `master`; the evidence commit it was pinned to (`2d0ca9d`) is likewise absent from
`master`; `SyncPointDigest`'s required inputs (all GPRs, every implemented CSR) cannot be sourced
from `RetireRecord`, the only trace format this task's blocker (#390) actually defines; the null
family's real dependency, `jls.mach`, was cited only as an unnumbered "TASK-0070" though it is
filed and open as **#477**; "assert the report text" had no pinned grammar and was satisfiable
vacuously; and the pitest scope that is supposed to hold the reporting path accountable does not
include `jls.parity`. The visionary review (verdict: endorse-with-reframing) endorsed
first-divergence reporting, the never-a-pass verdict lattice, and the refusal of a constant-zero
null outright, and reframed four things: let the record's own declared field list be the comparison
alphabet instead of an exclusion set subtracted from an assumed universe; make the verdict a sealed
hierarchy that forces every non-pass to carry its evidence, not a bare enum; replace the four
hand-carved null implementations with the project's already-adopted PIT mutation apparatus; and
build the report as a small shared `jls.report` package rather than a private formatter inside
`jls.parity`.

The body below **is** the fix and the redirect together. It is also brought into line with this
task's own parent feature, **#347 (FEAT-034)**, which was independently reviewed and rewritten
(2026-08-08 through 2026-08-10) and already names "TASK-0073 (revised)" as: a comparator emitting
`PASS` / `FAIL(k, field)` / `UNKNOWN`; a rolling digest at a fixed retirement stride for
boot-length runs (checkpoint-bounded I/O, not trace-length-bounded); bisection into the first
differing interval on divergence, usable against the *existing* `riscv/verify.py` final-state
comparator before the trace format lands; and an exclusion-set ratchet shipped **capped at zero
entries**, grown only by an explicit maintainer decision recorded in the same commit as the growth.
That is the design instantiated here — it happens to satisfy the visionary review's exclusion-set
concern by a different, already-decided mechanism (cap at zero, not "delete the mechanism
entirely"), and its PIT-based null test is exactly Reframing C. Where #347's redirect and this
issue's own reviews agree, they are merged into one design rather than presented as two competing
ones.

### Unabsorbed review findings (recorded 2026-08-16)

The 2026-08-08 dual-lens review raised the following points that this body neither adopts nor
explicitly declines. Recorded pending maintainer disposition; recording is not endorsement.

- **Visionary review**, "Where it pulls against the arc" point 4 / Reframing C: recommended
  harvesting `riscv/fuzz_diff.py`'s random program generator into `test/` before #413 deletes
  `riscv/`, arguing the generator (not `build_cpu.py`) is the reusable asset. This body's §1 (Background & Prior Work) and
  § Related Work only treat `riscv/` as a read-only interim bisect target for #413's deletion and
  never mention `fuzz_diff.py` or porting its generator.

## Abstract

Two traces without a comparator are two files. This task builds `src/jls/parity`'s comparator and
a small shared `src/jls/report` package: a `TraceDiffer` that reports **the first differing
retirement index, both records side by side, and the names of the differing fields**; a `Verdict`
sealed over `ParityHeld | DivergedAtIndex(k, recordD, recordP, fields) | NotComparable(cause) |
Unknown(reason)`, whose `isPass()` is a pattern switch with no `default` arm, true only for
`ParityHeld`, and where `NotComparable`/`Unknown` cannot be filed without naming *why*; an exclusion
set that ships **at cap zero** and can only grow via an explicit maintainer decision plus a ratchet
update in the same commit; a `SyncPointDigest` over full architectural state (sourced from
`jls.mach`'s `ArchState`, not from the twelve-field `RetireRecord`, which was never meant to carry
it); a `-diff-against FILE` flag; and a null family built on the project's already-adopted PIT
mutation apparatus rather than four hand-picked faults, backed by one committed golden report
transcript so "assert the report text" cannot be satisfied by a formatter that prints everything.
A differ that reports "traces differ" has done nothing `cmp` could not; first-divergence reporting
is the whole product.

## Intended Audience & Impact

- **Anyone who claims a drawn CPU agrees with a reference.** The claim becomes checkable at the
  exact instruction and the exact field, instead of "the run failed".
- **A student verifying a design they did not write.** A differential oracle is the only honest
  acceptance test for an unfamiliar core, and #369 (autograding, via #483/TASK-0112's equivalence
  check) is the same machinery aimed at a submission.
- **A reviewer reading a green check.** The null family is what makes the check mean something: an
  implementation that survives every mutant proves only that the harness is connected and does not
  count, and the mutation-testing apparatus this task retargets already enforces that.
- **Anyone reading a parity report.** The exclusion set is printed in every report, because an
  exclusion a user cannot see is policy hidden in comparison code — and it starts empty, so today
  there is nothing hidden to print but the empty set itself.

## Abstract

Accessible-name coverage over JLS's Swing chrome is currently enforced by nothing at build time: a focusable widget built outside the `labelled(...)` naming funnel does not fail `mvn verify`, and `docs/keyboard-a11y-verification.md`'s rows cite tests by name with no mechanism asserting those citations still resolve. This task adds a headless, always-blocking construction-time gate — reusing the `NotificationRatchetTest`/`DialogCoverageRatchetTest` scan idiom and #756's `ElementFormDialog` construction-audit surface — for the naming predicate #756 explicitly leaves unchecked, and turns the doc into a two-way-checked catalog (the `ExtensionPointCatalogTest` idiom) with three explicit row categories (`automated`/`manual`/`exception`) instead of prose that can drift silently from the tests it cites.

## Intended Audience & Impact

- **Contributors and maintainers (including LLM agents) landing UI changes.** Today, deleting or renaming a test that `docs/keyboard-a11y-verification.md` cites, or constructing a new focusable widget outside `labelled(...)`, produces no red build anywhere — confirmed below (§2, Observations): no test class enforces either property in this checkout. After this task, both fail `mvn verify` immediately, before the change ships.
- **Downstream: keyboard-only and assistive-technology users of the editor chrome** (the audience #75 and #549 exist for). This task adds no new user-facing behavior itself; it protects the accessible-name guarantee #75 already shipped from silently regressing. Framed per the audience guidance: this is internal CI/test tooling whose sole beneficiary is the accessibility guarantee already delivered to keyboard-only and screen-reader users of the palette, dialogs, and menus.

## Abstract

The CheerpJ-vs-SVG+VCD mechanism choice for the browser demo (CAP-32, #516) is already decided — CheerpJ rejected outright, the SVG-plus-precomputed-lookup-table/VCD mechanism adopted, and TASK-C572-1 (#833)/TASK-C572-2 (#835) are the tasks scoped to build and confirm it (both are still `blocked_by` dependencies of this task, and their landed state is not verified anywhere in this body — § 11 (Threats to Validity)) — but that decision currently lives only in issue-tracker prose (#516's Direction argument), not in-tree. ## Abstract

## Abstract

`jls.core` has no width-carrying signal value type: the simulator's currency is a bare, mutable, width-less `java.util.BitSet`, threaded through 61 defensive clone sites across `src/jls/elem` and `src/jls/sim`. This is the first of two children #232 needs, and it lands only the type: an immutable, width-carrying, three-plane signal value (`sealed interface LogicValue permits Word, Wide`) in `jls.core`, with its operation set, its equality contract, its coverage floor, and its tests — and **no call site outside `jls.core` changes**, with one named exception (§7.4, alphabet reservation). Widening the plumbing, deleting the 61 clones, and retiring the `null`-as-HiZ channel is TASK-C232-2 (#879)'s job; keeping the two tasks separate is what makes #879's byte-identity claim attributable to the plumbing change alone rather than to a simultaneous representation change.

## Intended Audience & Impact

This task is internal groundwork with no directly observable change for students, instructors, or `.jls`-file tooling at landing: P8 (§5) constrains the diff to `src/jls/core`, `test/jls/core`, `pom.xml`, plus one named accessor pair, so the `.jls` file format, CLI/batch (`-b`) behaviour, the GUI, and every existing simulation result are unchanged.

- **Contributors and LLM agents executing #879 (the plumbing widening) and #322 (four-state semantics).** They get a frozen, measured, tested value type to build against instead of having to settle the representation mid-migration. #419 (radix validation) and #422 (the higher-radix op set) are specified against this task's op set; #391 (the resolution fold) states its own local pair "is deliberately shaped to match" this task's frozen layout.
- **Downstream, eventually students and instructors**, once #879/#322 make this type the simulator's live currency: today `docs/simulation-semantics.md` §2 is titled "Value domain: two states plus HiZ" and states plainly "There is no unknown/X state anywhere in the simulator" — this task is what makes a later landing able to change that. That visible change belongs to #322/#888, not to this task; nothing here is visible to a circuit author.
- **Maintainers reviewing the representation decision.** §7's Frozen field list is the record of a measured choice (O6) so the decision does not have to be re-litigated by a future reader who only sees the diff.

## Status & Dependencies

owned_by_derived: [232]  # DERIVED from feature rosters, NOT authoritative;

  - 362   # FEAT-030 — this is the leg its planned_tasks calls "TASK-0056"
  - 391   # TASK-0057 — the resolution fold; its local two-plane pair is "deliberately shaped to match" this frozen layout

## 1. Background & Prior Work

Two roadmap documents on `master` propose a value type and are, as of this task, stale on **representation** (not on sequencing): `docs/capability-roadmap/keystone-b-migration.md` line 535 specifies `jls.core.LogicVector`, a sealed interface with a `Binary` case (one `BitSet` plane) and a `FourState` case (aval/bval two-plane, IEEE 1364 `s_vpi_vecval` encoding); `docs/capability-roadmap/sweep-01-values-and-logic.md` §V1 (heading at line 87, "A per-bit four-state value type (`0 / 1 / X / Z`) replacing `@Nullable BitSet`") specifies the same two-plane aval/bval shape as "the representation that costs least and is best-precedented."

`docs/capability-roadmap/keystone-c-performance.md` measured five representations (R0–R4) against JLS's actual hot-loop access pattern and rejects the two-plane shape on performance grounds, independent of the design-grounds rejection keystone A already made (§2, below). `docs/capability-roadmap/README.md:134-136` records the three-plane shape — `sealed interface LogicValue permits Word, Wide` — as the already-committed roadmap decision that follows from that measurement.

This task's direct successor, #879 (TASK-C232-2), is already filed against this exact type: its `blocked_by` names #878 with "No waiver is available for this edge... #878 landing is a hard gate," and its own §3 states waiving that dependency "would require this task to invent its own ad hoc replacement for `null`." #879 also already narrows its own scope away from a `T4`-labelled javadoc note this task's Out-of-Scope section once assumed existed (see Open Questions, item 3) — #879's current §7 ("`Adder`'s carry — a type op, not a javadoc note") instead commits to a `LogicValue.addCarry` op, sourced from this task if it exists by #879's pickup.

`sealed interface Payload` in `src/jls/sim/SimEvent.java` (line 23) is the existing in-tree precedent for the sealed-interface-plus-records pattern this task's `LogicValue` follows.

**O1 — there is no width-carrying value type.** `git show c5cee1baff3451a85787b4a09bd0b2b05af7dfdd:src/jls/core` lists exactly: `Bounds.java`, `Geometry.java`, `GridPoint.java`, `GridSize.java`, `Orientation.java`, `SegmentGeometry.java`, `TextMetrics.java`, `package-info.java`. ## Proposed disposition

The visionary-lens review (2026-08-08, verdict: **endorse-with-reframing**) endorses this feature's goal without reservation — JLS's HDL emitters have no counterparty, and a semantically wrong emitter reaches a student today — but argues the one architectural choice this issue made, routing the correctness guarantee through CI toolchain arming, pulls against the rest of the project, where every other contract is pinned by a committed golden. The adversarial-lens review (2026-08-08, verdict: **needs-rework**) separately found that the criterion this reframing targets (criterion 2, "a knowingly wrong emitter is caught") was gameable as written, that the feature's own evidence corpus (`docs/plan/`, `docs/parity-contract.md`) does not exist in this repository, and that TASK-0052's ownership contest between this issue and #264 was self-documented as unresolved. A maintainer directive of 2026-08-16 subsequently overruled the committed-trace inversion those reviews produced: the authoritative check is cross-simulator agreement, gating.

Per this pass's disposition rule, no issue is closed, merged, or split to enact either review. Instead:

- **The correctness guarantee is cross-simulator agreement, and it gates (maintainer directive 2026-08-16, superseding the 2026-08-08 committed-trace inversion).** For each corpus fixture — a design plus a stimulus in the existing `-t` batch grammar — every available backend produces a dump: JLS's own `BatchSimulator`, plus each provisioned external simulator run over the emitted HDL. The build gates on all available backends agreeing; any divergence is a red build demanding critical investigation, because a divergence where both outputs look plausible means someone has a bug — an important finding in itself. A backend-declared `x` is **UNCONSTRAINED** — it cannot contradict anything — and is reported as a per-run coverage-gap rate, not forced into a pass or a fail. CI provisions the external toolchains and is the enforcement point; on machines lacking a toolchain the external legs skip with a visible notice, never silently. Arming (TASK-0051/#386) stays infrastructure hygiene rather than this feature's correctness guarantee, and is bound into CAP-15's (#310) own closure via that capstone's `requires_tasks_exception`. This is the same three-verdict (AGREE / DIVERGE / UNCONSTRAINED) comparator CAP-15 (#310) §1 (Outcome Statement) step 2 / AC-1 specify — feature tier and capstone tier now agree on one design.
- **TASK-0052 (the second board plus the hardware flash) is struck from this issue's roster and its ownership question resolved in favor of #264.** Both #416 (TASK-0052 as filed) and #264 independently recommend this same resolution as their own default; #264's "Remaining scope, per board" and Definition of Done are the actual source of that work. This issue does not duplicate #264's board on-ramp. The edits #416 and #264 each need to reflect this are reported in this pass's bookkeeping, not made here — see the caller's `other_issue_edits`.
- **TASK-0100 (the analog/ngspice differential corpus) is confirmed as FEAT-046's own roster item, filed as #397, not this issue's.** This issue references it as a sibling using the same locator/skip/lane machinery; it does not count its weeks or claim its criteria.
- **Criterion 2 is tightened so it cannot be satisfied by a one-time demonstration** (adversarial finding 4): the deliverable is a permanent, named regression-test class that runs on every build, not a screenshot of a red CI run followed by a revert.
- **The evidence corpus this issue was pinned to is confirmed gone, and its citations are repointed rather than deleted** (adversarial finding 1). `docs/plan/` and `docs/parity-contract.md` were removed from every branch this repository merges (commit `742da745`, "the maintainer ruled that this branch will not be merged and will be deleted"); #493 is the durable pin for code-level citations, and #495 preserves `docs/parity-contract.md` in full — but that document is **explicitly unratified** ("binds nothing yet ... nothing in the repository currently implements any mechanism it governs"), which is a harder problem than a missing file: the permitted-to-differ framing this feature's differential leg needs was never settled even on the branch that wrote it.

Everything below states this issue's current intent under that redirection. It does not narrate how the issue arrived here.

## Abstract

JLS's two HDL emitters — `VerilogEmitter` and `VhdlEmitter` — are checked today only against goldens JLS itself wrote, and the external-tool legs that exist (`IverilogCompileTest`, `GhdlCompileTest`) check that those goldens *parse*, not that they *mean* what the drawn circuit means. A sign flip in an emitted assignment compiles perfectly and reaches a student. This feature closes that gap with a **gating agreement comparator** (maintainer directive 2026-08-16): for each corpus fixture — a design plus a committed stimulus in the existing `-t` batch grammar — every available backend produces a VCD dump: JLS's own `BatchSimulator`, and each provisioned external simulator (`iverilog`, `ghdl`, `verilator`) run over the emitted HDL. All dumps are compared at settling points — the stimulus fixture's own declared event times plus a settle epsilon — with a three-verdict comparator: **AGREE** (values match), **DIVERGE** (two backends disagree on a definite `0`/`1`/`z`), **UNCONSTRAINED** (a backend emitted `x`, which cannot contradict anything — a coverage gap reported as a per-run rate, not a pass or a fail). The build gates on all available backends agreeing; any DIVERGE is a red build demanding critical investigation, because a divergence where both outputs look plausible means someone has a bug — an important finding in itself. CI provisions the external toolchains and is the enforcement point; on a machine lacking a toolchain the external legs skip with a visible notice, never silently.

## Abstract

The README carries no positioning content against the four closest incumbent
tools (Logisim-Evolution, Digital, CircuitVerse, Falstad) and exactly one
badge (OpenSSF Scorecard), a supply-chain signal aimed at auditors rather
than at a prospective student or instructor. This task adds a short,
evidence-checked "use something else if" routing paragraph plus a capped
comparison table, authored once in a structured source and rendered into
both the README and #553's switcher pages behind a drift check, and adds at
least one new user-facing badge. It implements #545 (FEAT-C27-1) AC-3
(positioning section) and AC-4 (badge signals) for the four named
competitors only; #545's own text is canonical if this summary and that
issue ever disagree.

## Abstract

JLS's editor palette holds 32 loadable element types
([`Palette.entries()`](https://github.com/anadon/JLS/blob/c5cee1baff3451a85787b4a09bd0b2b05af7dfdd/src/jls/edit/Palette.java#L232-L234),
backed by the [`ENTRIES` table](https://github.com/anadon/JLS/blob/c5cee1baff3451a85787b4a09bd0b2b05af7dfdd/src/jls/edit/Palette.java#L123-L188))
but no way to reach one by typing its name — Logisim-Evolution's
oldest cited findability complaint (upstream Logisim-Evolution issue
1234, external, not re-verified by this migration), closed here inside
#594's
keyboard-invoked command surface. This task builds that surface's
first item source: an incremental, deterministic search over each
entry's display name
([`PaletteEntry.tooltip()`](https://github.com/anadon/JLS/blob/c5cee1baff3451a85787b4a09bd0b2b05af7dfdd/src/jls/edit/PaletteEntry.java#L145-L147))
and a new GUI-side synonym table, plus a no-match state that redirects
a curated list of first-year misnomers ("flip-flop", "demux", …) to
the part JLS actually calls them. The index reads through
`Palette.entries()` rather than `ElementRegistry` directly, so a
module-gated type stays out of search exactly as it stays off the
toolbar (#482), and it is a model-side collaborator built lazily on
first overlay invocation — never a `SimpleEditor` field, never a
startup cost.

## Intended Audience & Impact

**Students drawing and simulating circuits in the editor** — concretely,
per the old body's own framing, a user "who knows what a part is called"
but not where it lives on the toolbar, including switchers from
Logisim-Evolution, Digital, or CircuitVerse who bring that incumbent's
vocabulary with them (a Logisim-Evolution user typing "flip-flop"
expecting a hit, when JLS's own registered name is `Register` —
confirmed as a real registered tag at
[`ElementRegistry.java:61`](https://github.com/anadon/JLS/blob/c5cee1baff3451a85787b4a09bd0b2b05af7dfdd/src/jls/elem/ElementRegistry.java#L61),
`new ElementType("Register", Register.class, Register::new)`, and as a
real palette row at
[`Palette.java:158-159`](https://github.com/anadon/JLS/blob/c5cee1baff3451a85787b4a09bd0b2b05af7dfdd/src/jls/edit/Palette.java#L158-L159)
with tooltip `"register (various triggering)"`). Today that user has
no path to a part by typing at all — the only paths are the fixed
32-entry toolbar grid grouped by `Palette.Group`
(`Palette.entries()`), or the mirrored "elements" `JMenu` that
`SimpleEditor.makeElements()`
([`SimpleEditor.java:2306`](https://github.com/anadon/JLS/blob/c5cee1baff3451a85787b4a09bd0b2b05af7dfdd/src/jls/edit/SimpleEditor.java#L2306))
builds and that is added as a submenu of the empty-space right-click
popup at
[`SimpleEditor.java:1358`](https://github.com/anadon/JLS/blob/c5cee1baff3451a85787b4a09bd0b2b05af7dfdd/src/jls/edit/SimpleEditor.java#L1358)
(`newMenu.add(elementsMenu);`) — that popup being the field
doc-commented `/** Right-click menu over empty space. */` and declared
at
[`SimpleEditor.java:1181-1182`](https://github.com/anadon/JLS/blob/c5cee1baff3451a85787b4a09bd0b2b05af7dfdd/src/jls/edit/SimpleEditor.java#L1181-L1182)
(`private JPopupMenu newMenu = new JPopupMenu();`), reachable only by
right-click. This task's landing does not itself make that surface
keyboard-reachable (#808 owns that) or add recency ranking (#941 owns
that); what it delivers, on its own, is that once the overlay exists
at all, typing a part's tooltip or a listed synonym returns it, and
typing a wrong-but-common name for a right part explains the mismatch
instead of returning nothing. The gap this closes is measurable in the
narrowest sense available pre-implementation: no class in `src/jls`
today does any form of palette text search (§2, Observation 4) — the
capability is currently absent, not merely incomplete.

## Abstract

The original ask behind this task — let a `Text` annotation element use a monospace font — is already shipped: `Text` has per-element `fontName`/`fontSize`/`isBold`/`isItalic`, persisted through the declarative `Attribute` mechanism, selectable in `TextDialog`'s font-family combo (which always offers the JDK logical family `"Monospaced"`), and drawn through the identical `TextRenderer` code path in both the editor canvas and the `-i` SVG export. Nothing in the shipped code needs to change. What remains fundable here is narrower: a regression test that pins that already-existing behavior (so it cannot silently regress), while a genuinely open defect this task's earlier drafts conflated with it — `SwingTextMetrics.defaultFontName()` baking a resolved, platform-specific host UI font name into the persisted `fn` field — is redirected to #536/#76, where it belongs.

## Intended Audience & Impact

- **Students and circuit-file authors** annotating circuits with `Text` elements (e.g. bus-width labels, pinout notes) that benefit from a fixed-width face: this already works today (§2 (Observations) Obs. 1–4); no audience-visible change ships from this task.
- **Contributors and maintainers** reviewing future changes to `Text`, `TextDialog`, or the SVG export path: a regression test converts "this already works" from an unverified claim in an issue thread into an executable guarantee that a future refactor cannot silently break, and that a future `.jls` save-format change cannot silently corrupt (AC-2, byte-identical default-face saves).
- **Instructors and graders in batch (`-b`) mode**: byte-identical save output for `Text`-bearing circuits (AC-2) protects checked-in graded fixture files from spurious diffs.
- Out of scope for this task's audience: anyone affected by the font-*identity*-portability gap (a `.jls` file's `fn` field recording e.g. `"Segoe UI"` on Windows vs. a GTK face on Linux) — that audience is served by #536 (bundled deterministic font path) and #76 (font/theme visual-ergonomics umbrella), not here.

## Abstract

JLS has no oracle that proves a run's observable output — the watched-element stdout stream and the VCD waveform dump — is a function of the design alone, independent of how the run was arranged: repeated single-JVM runs, the JDK 25 / advisory-newest-GA CI lane pair, the three-OS CI lanes, and (once its four prerequisite issues land) partition counts 1, 2, 4 and 8. This task builds that oracle as a re-keyed `BatchSimulator.getTraceSamples()` equality (not a byte diff), wires it against every arrangement axis that is buildable today, and adds a structural (ArchUnit) ratchet that no output artefact can carry which arrangement produced it. It is a rewrite, not a new task: it keeps designator TASK-C333-5 and parent #333, replaces a self-defeating byte-diff oracle and a gameable grep-based leak check the two 2026-08-08 reviews found in the prior body, and generalizes the axis from "partition count" (not yet buildable) to "execution arrangement" (mostly buildable now).

## Intended Audience & Impact

- **Contributors, maintainers, and LLM agents working the codebase.** Today a regression that makes JLS's output depend on incidental arrangement — a seed/iteration-order bug, a platform-specific line ending, a JDK-version-sensitive `HashMap` iteration — has no automated tripwire beyond what `SimulationSeedOrderTest` already covers for one narrow case. This task is the general tripwire: it runs on every push once landed (AC-6) and names its failures at the signal and sample, not a byte offset.
- **Anyone running a golden suite in batch (`-b`) mode**, per #333's own Intended Audience & Impact: a distributed or platform-varying run that answers differently from a whole run destroys the golden discipline exactly where hand-checking is impossible. This task is the first concrete evidence-gathering step toward that guarantee, landing the two axes (repeated-run, JDK/OS) that need nothing else to exist first.
- **#312 (CAP-17)**, transitively through #333: this task is #333's named evidence artefact (`requires_tasks: [830, 832, 834, 838, 839]` in #333's machine block) for the capstone's "simulates as one design across a cluster" mechanism. It does not itself prove partition-count invariance (that axis is gated — see Boundary notes) but it proves the oracle and the two arrangement axes that do not depend on partitioning existing.

## Abstract

Once TASK-C577-1 (#761) lands a provenance manifest for the CSE 260M corpus, nothing in the required build actually walks it: a fixture can silently drop out of the corpus, or a real behavioral regression can be waved away in a free-text comment, and `mvn verify` stays green either way. This task adds `test/jls/CorpusConformanceTest.java` to the required suite — no new CI workflow — which loads and simulates every fixture named by every `test/conformance/*/MANIFEST` it finds, diffs each transcript-bearing fixture's normalized batch output against its captured origin-fork run, asserts a `load-only` fixture merely settles, and fails the build on any load failure, any undisposed diff, or a shrinking manifest row count. ## Abstract

The in-app help viewer (`jls.Help`) has no way to show a human-shareable
address for the page a reader is looking at, and the "hosted docs are the
planned future" story in `ARCHITECTURE.md` still describes a design JLS
never adopted. This task adds a pure, headless-testable rule that turns a
running version plus a topic id into a URL on the hosted manual, surfaces
that URL as copyable text in the viewer with a non-blocking "open in
browser" affordance, gives the hosted site the same link-integrity
discipline the in-jar tree already has from `HelpTopicsTest`, ships one
build-time search index consumed by both surfaces, and corrects the stale
`ARCHITECTURE.md` claim that the in-app viewer will eventually "shrink."

## Intended Audience & Impact

- **Students and instructors using the GUI.** `jls.Help` is reached only
  from Swing menu items and dialog Help buttons (`Help.showTopic("top")`
  at [`src/jls/JLSStart.java:2177`](https://github.com/anadon/JLS/blob/c5cee1baff3451a85787b4a09bd0b2b05af7dfdd/src/jls/JLSStart.java#L2177),
  and `Help.enableHelpOnButton` calls from
  `src/jls/edit/InteractiveSimulator.java:156`,
  `src/jls/edit/ElementFormDialog.java:190`,
  `src/jls/edit/TruthTableEditor.java:103`, and
  `src/jls/edit/StateMachineDialog.java:397`) — there is no batch (`-b`)
  mode surface. Today a student or instructor who wants to paste a help
  page into a syllabus or a bug report has no address to paste at all;
  after this task they get one that resolves and resolves to the version

## Abstract

This issue is the genuine, currently-unclaimed residual of #76 and #73's scaling verification: whether the editor renders correctly at an arbitrary composed scale — zoom × display scale factor (`uiScale`) — asserted by tests rather than a hand-run screenshot matrix across four platforms and three scale factors. `.github/workflows/ci.yml` already boots and screenshots the real application on Linux (Wayland/JBR and X11/Xvfb), macOS (WindowServer) and Windows (WindowStation) on every push, which closes the matrix's platform dimension; the missing dimension is scale factor, which is a JVM system property (`-Dsun.java2d.uiScale`), not a hardware requirement. What remains after that correction is: threading the property through the existing `@Tag("display")` suite, two new assertions (dialog layout-fit under scale, hit-testing under a fractional transform), and a three-line addition to the project's existing per-release manual checklist for the handful of things a headless rig genuinely cannot reach (compositor-level fractional scaling, FlatLaf's custom window decorations, macOS backing-store behavior). The dark theme variant, the welcome panel and bundled samples, the README pass, and the icon/chrome cleanup — this issue's other four original workstreams — are filed and better-specified elsewhere (#289; the #511/CAP-27 cluster via #550/#548/#545 and their sub-tasks; #287 and #286 respectively) and are not this issue's work. ## Intended Audience & Impact

- **Students and instructors** on a fractionally-scaled or HiDPI display: a clipped dialog, or a hit-test that stops agreeing with drawn geometry at `uiScale` 1.25, fails CI instead of shipping unnoticed.

## Abstract

A port's owner is typed as the reacting element, not as any element: [`Put.java:25`](https://github.com/anadon/JLS/blob/c5cee1baff3451a85787b4a09bd0b2b05af7dfdd/src/jls/elem/Put.java#L25) declares `protected @Nullable LogicElement element;`, so nothing outside the `LogicElement` sealed hierarchy can own a terminal. Net propagation then launders that assumption through a cast: [`WireNet.java:507`](https://github.com/anadon/JLS/blob/c5cee1baff3451a85787b4a09bd0b2b05af7dfdd/src/jls/elem/WireNet.java#L507) posts `new SimEvent(now, (Reacts) element, ...)`, so a future non-reacting `Element` placed on a net would be silently handed a pin-change payload it has no contract to receive, rather than refused or skipped. ## Abstract

`jls -aggregate` — the pure, single-threaded fold that turns a job list and a directory of per-job receipts into one campaign report — does not exist yet: no `-aggregate` entry appears in `JLSStart`'s flag table, no aggregator source exists anywhere in the tree, and no report format is documented. This is the entire correctness content of FEAT-057 (#350) §3's commutativity claim ($A(J;\sigma,w)=A(J;\sigma',w')$ for every dispatch order $\sigma$ and worker count $w$): the claim is unverifiable and unenforceable until this program exists, because there is currently nothing for a randomized-order test to run against. The remedy is a separate, single-threaded `jls -aggregate joblist receipts-dir` entry point that looks up each job's receipt by digest and folds strictly in job-list order, with an import/API-absence ratchet making worker count, dispatch order, and completion order structurally unobservable rather than merely absent by convention, emitting a golden-pinned xUnit XML report (plus a plain line format) whose `tests` count is always the job-list length.

## Intended Audience & Impact

- **Instructors and course staff running campaigns** (parameter sweeps, fault-injection runs, cohort submission sets) across cores or hosts via an external dispatcher (`xargs -P`, `make -j`, GNU parallel, a Slurm array — #350's own scope boundary). Today there is no `-aggregate` flag at all: `JLSStart`'s flag table ([`src/jls/JLSStart.java` L759–L789](https://github.com/anadon/JLS/blob/c5cee1baff3451a85787b4a09bd0b2b05af7dfdd/src/jls/JLSStart.java#L759-L789)) has no entry whose `flag` field is `"aggregate"` or a prefix of it, so nothing in JLS folds N receipts into one report — every instructor who wants that today must hand-roll it, which is exactly the risk #350 exists to eliminate structurally. This task is what makes that elimination real rather than aspirational.
- **Contributors and maintainers building on #350's family.** The grading harness (#369) is documented as consuming this feature's receipt/aggregate vocabulary as its per-item result record rather than inventing its own (#350 §1 point 3, "Resolved design decisions" item 1); multi-seed verification (#306) is a beneficial, non-required consumer of the same shape. Neither has anything to consume until this task lands.
- **Students**, indirectly: through #369's eventual verdict layer built on top of this aggregate, a correct campaign report is what lets "this ran on N workers in some order" become "this design passed or failed," without the grading result depending on incidental scheduling.

## Abstract

`examples/autograde/` today ships one Python bridge (`autograde.py`) that grades a single submission against one fixture; nothing in the tree walks a whole cohort, and nothing proves that a malformed, missing, renamed, or unmatched submission is reported as a named result rather than shrinking the result count or aborting the run. candidates.body:
## Summary

Promotes the #161 report-only PIT trial to a blocking climb-ratchet (#159): the `pitest` Maven profile now carries `mutationThreshold` 80 / `testStrengthThreshold` 82 over the scoped core (`jls.sim.*`, `jls.BitSetUtils`, `jls.Util`, `jls.SpatialIndex`, `jls.collab.op.*`), and the weekly `mutation.yml` run fails on a breach instead of swallowing it.

## What / why

- **`pom.xml` (pitest profile only)**: adds `mutationThreshold` 80 and `testStrengthThreshold` 82, with a comment block recording the baseline measurement and the climb convention (floors only ever move up, raised with the PR that raises the score, >=2pt headroom under the worst of 3 clean headless canonical-JDK-25 runs). The JaCoCo ratchet section is untouched.
- **`.github/workflows/mutation.yml`**: `continue-on-error` removed from the `mutationCoverage` step so a threshold breach turns the weekly run red; the PIT report upload gains `if: always()` so a breaching run stays diagnosable. The workflow remains schedule + `workflow_dispatch` only and is never a required PR check.
- **`CONTRIBUTING.md`**: the Mutation-testing-status bullet is rewritten to the promoted state (edit confined to that bullet; disjoint from #96's Conventions-list region — union merge acceptable on rebase).
- **`docs/mutation-testing-trial-2026-07.md`**: dated promotion addendum with the measurement table, scope-shift note (trial's 1173 mutants vs ~900 now — same `targetClasses`, the code moved), workflow change, and non-vacuity probe.
- **`CHANGELOG.md`**: entry under Unreleased.

Per the cycle adjudication, thresholds were floored from the worst of three runs on a tree with #167 (`feat/167-partial-net-delete` @ 19f561b, which grows `jls.collab.op` inside PIT scope) merged locally: 752/905 = 83.09%, then 751/905 = 82.98% twice; test strength 84.78% / 84.67% / 84.67% (jitter ~0.1pt). A pre-#167 3x measurement (726/881 = 82.40% / 84.12%, zero jitter) agreed within 0.7pt and yields the same floors.

## Verification (independent re-run by reviewer)

All via `nix develop path:… --command bash -c '…'`, headless, JDK 25:

- `mvn -B clean verify` in the worktree: **BUILD SUCCESS** — surefire `Tests run: 1192, Failures: 0, Errors: 0, Skipped: 5`; failsafe 92 display-tagged tests all skipped headless (expected); `All coverage checks have been met` (JaCoCo ratchet unaffected).
- `mvn -B -Ppitest clean test-compile org.pitest:pitest-maven:mutationCoverage` on the branch: **BUILD SUCCESS** with thresholds active — `Generated 881 mutations Killed 726 (82%)`, `Test strength 84%` (exactly reproduces the implementer's bare-base numbers).
- Non-vacuity probe (independently repeated): `mutationThreshold` temporarily set to 95 → **BUILD FAILURE**, `Mutation score of 82 is below threshold of 95`; reverted.
- Adjudication check (independently repeated once): scratch worktree merging this branch with `feat/167-partial-net-delete` @ 19f561b → **BUILD SUCCESS** with thresholds active — `Generated 905 mutations Killed 751 (83%)`, `Test strength 85%`, matching the implementer's worst-of-three (751/905 = 82.98%).
- pitest-maven 1.25.8 supports both threshold parameters (verified empirically by the binding probe).

## Caveats

- **This PR must merge LAST this cycle** (after #167): the thresholds were baselined on a tree including #167's `jls.collab.op` growth. If #167 is amended/rebased with further `jls.collab.op` changes beyond 19f561b, re-run the 3x measurement post-merge — though the floors carry ~2.9pt slack, so small deltas will not move them.
- PIT reports integer scores, so the probe error says "score of 82" (82.98 truncated) — expected.
- The `testStrengthThreshold` was not separately probed for non-vacuity, but PIT enforces both thresholds through the same mechanism and the mutation-threshold probe demonstrated the gate binds.
- Commit is unsigned (sandbox constraint) — re-sign via `git commit --amend` before push.

## Abstract

At `c5cee1b` (re-verified 2026-08-16 against the current default-branch tip — the previously
pinned `646d5ae`/`2d0ca9d` is not an ancestor of `master` and is corrected here, same citation
defect as #335; every cited file is byte-identical between the two commits, so no citation
below changed) the token `longrun` does not appear anywhere in the repository outside
`issue-reviews/`, `.github/workflows/` contains no `timeout-minutes` at all, and no rule
anywhere states how large a tracked fixture may be. This task gives the required pull-request
gate a stated, falsifiable wall-clock budget; gives a large fixture a declared, tiered storage
policy with a non-vacuous ratchet; and gives an hours-long test a way to run that is not the
required gate — not by adding a scheduled `longrun.yml` cron that hosts a single multi-hour job
(the original design), but by decomposing it into a **checkpoint-chain** of ordinary,
job-timeout-sized segments built on FEAT-035/#363's resume-by-replay primitive
(`-checkpoint-at`, a four-field resume token, SIGINT-safe recording), invoked on demand rather
than hosted by a standing lane. #317 (FEAT-007), the owning feature, redirected this task's
long-run half to exactly this shape in its own 2026-08-09 revision and named this issue as
needing the matching follow-up edit; this rewrite is that edit.

## Intended Audience & Impact

- **Contributors and maintainers.** Today a multi-hour acceptance test cannot be written,
  because writing it makes every pull request take hours. Afterwards it can be written as a
  checkpoint-chain of bounded segments, invoked by `workflow_dispatch`, a release tag, or a PR
  label, without lengthening a single pull request and without a standing scheduled job that
  nobody triages.
- **Every downstream plan item that needs a long run**: the headless boot run (#326), the
  nightly analog corpus, the calibration measurement runs (#335/FEAT-009). Each currently has
  nowhere to execute; each gains a segmentation pattern to execute against instead of a single
  unbounded job.
- **Students cloning the repository.** The fixture cap is stated in terms of what a clone costs
  on a slow link, not a hosting provider's limits, and is measured on the bytes the fixture
  actually costs a `git clone` — compressed, since every current fixture is text and Git already
  deflates it — not on-disk bytes, which overstate that cost by roughly 20x for the fixture that
  sets today's number (see Observations, O6).

## Status & Dependencies

related: [335, 202, 265, 111, 386, 354]
                        # 386 TASK-0051: edits the same .github/workflows/ci.yml file and was

                        # 354 FEAT-006: not a blocker for this task, but the ceiling removals it

## Abstract

At `c5cee1baff3451a85787b4a09bd0b2b05af7dfdd`, there is not one `timeout-minutes` anywhere under
`.github/workflows/`, across 23 jobs in 6 files (verified directly at this commit, below — this
migration re-derived every citation fresh rather than trusting the prior filing's multi-commit
provenance chain). The absence is not "no limit": it is GitHub's hosted default of 360 minutes,
applied silently, and `concurrency.cancel-in-progress` only cancels on a *new* push to the same
ref, so a hang on `master` is cancelled by nothing.

This task gives every job a `timeout-minutes` drawn from one of four fixed archetype ceilings (not
derived per-job from a manually-read run-history table — see Background), gives every
network-fetch step its own step timeout strictly below its job's bound so a stalled download is
attributed to the download, and adds `scripts/workflow-policy-check.sh` — a check run as its own
CI step (not inside `mvn verify`) — that fails when a job lacks a timeout, a `uses:` reference is
not SHA-pinned, or a workflow lacks a top-level `permissions:` block. All three properties already
hold today (0/23 timeouts is the one gap; 70/70 `uses:` refs are already SHA-pinned and all 6 files
already declare top-level `permissions:`), so the check locks in two properties for free while
closing the one that's missing. This migration also found that the previously-recorded premise
"PyYAML is available in the build-tooling environment" does not reproduce here — see O6 (revised)
and Open Questions.

## Intended Audience & Impact

- **Every contributor.** A wedged job today runs to the hosted ceiling and shows as in-progress the
  whole time. After this it is bounded by a number a reviewer can read in the workflow file, tied
  to a fixed, re-derivable archetype rather than a one-off manual measurement.
- **Packagers and distributors.** `release.yml` deliberately has no concurrency group
  (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:19-20`, issue #47), so its five jobs are the ones most exposed to a
  hang — and a release that hangs is a release that does not ship.
- **The capstones that need a long-run lane, via #317.** A long-run lane cannot be given a large
  budget honestly while the required lane has an implicit six-hour one.
- **Maintainers and LLM agents adding a workflow job.** The check turns "did you set a timeout?"
  from a review habit into a CI failure, and it turns "did you pin/scope this new `uses:` or
  `permissions:` block?" into the same failure, at no extra design cost.
- **#406**, whose own machine block (per the prior filing pass, not independently re-verified by
  this migration — see Open Questions) is stated to already read `blocked_by: [374]`: every job it
  touches (`windows`, `macos`) must arrive already bounded before it drops their advisory flag.

This is the cheapest item in its capstone chain and the one with the widest blast radius: it
changes nothing on a green run, which is precisely why the check matters more than the exact
values.

## Status & Dependencies

                        # citation below was re-derived directly at this commit via git show/
                        # git grep, not carried forward from an earlier pin unverified. A diff
                        # against the prior filing's 646d5ae pin over .github/workflows/ is empty
                        # (`git diff c5cee1baff3451a85787b4a09bd0b2b05af7dfdd 646d5ae805103947ac3a
                        # 6548caca12df5ec2b9c9 -- .github/workflows/`), so every job-key and
                        # step line number below matches the prior filing's numbers unchanged.

                        #   the owning features' requires_tasks are the only record.
                        #   Regenerate rather than hand-edit (validator G21).

  - 111                 # close-out: identical reasoning for the Windows lane

                        #   re-verified this pass — see Open Questions)
  - 378                 # stated to need this task's blocked_by edge added on its own side
                        #   (not independently re-verified this pass — see Open Questions)

**Preserved from the prior filing pass, not independently re-verified here.** A prior review pass
on this issue (dated 2026-08-08 in that pass's own record) recorded two review lenses — an
"adversarial" and a "visionary" reading — both endorsing this task's goal (every job gets an
explicit `timeout-minutes`, a standing check prevents a new one arriving without one) and neither
disputing the core defect. The visionary lens is recorded as recommending a scope split: ship the
bounding now as a small, mechanically-checkable change, and file the deeper "collapse 23
hand-written job blocks into ~6 `workflow_call` archetypes" refactor as separate future work — see
§13 (Conclusion & Future Work). That prior pass also recorded a correction: the sibling tasks this
issue's history calls "TASK-0016" and "TASK-0017" are said to already exist as **#378** and

could **not** independently re-verify #378's or #406's current machine-block contents against live
GitHub state in this pass — see Open Questions & Decisions Needed.

## Proposed disposition

The visionary-lens review (2026-08-08) argues this feature is sound in its stated goal but wrong as a single seam: it bundles a one-day repo-wide invariant, platform-lane promotion that duplicates two other features' filed slices, and a genuinely new capability whose right design is checkpoint-resume rather than a standing nightly lane. Its recommendation is to treat this as three efforts rather than one. Per this pass's disposition rule, none of the four already-filed child issues (#374, #378, #406, #411) is closed and no new issue is opened to enact the split. Instead the redirection is recorded directly in this issue's Decomposition, Capability Statement and Integration Criteria below: TASK-0015/#374 ships independently, but is no longer unchanged -- #374's own rewrite (2026-08-11) redirected its mechanism from a per-job history-read ritual to archetype-derived ceilings, from a Java `mvn verify` line-matcher to a standalone shell/Python policy check, and from a hardcoded file-count tripwire to an anti-vacuity check against an embedded known-bad fixture, and named the `workflow_call` archetype-collapse refactor as deferred future work rather than in-task scope; TASK-0017/#406's `ci.yml` edits are ceded to #265/#111's own filed slices, and #406 keeps only the promotion-ledger and coverage-ratchet decision; and TASK-0016/#378's long-run-lane half is redirected from a widened nightly cron to a checkpoint-chain capability built on #354 and #363. #378 and #406 still carry their original, un-redirected text as filed and need a follow-up edit of their own to match this redirection -- editing them is out of this issue's authority and is reported separately, not performed here.

## Abstract

Continuous integration gains the three properties a multi-hour capstone needs from it: every job carries an explicit `timeout-minutes`, so a hang costs minutes rather than the hosted six-hour ceiling; a run larger than one CI job is expressible as a checkpoint chain that resumes byte-identically -- rather than requiring a standing multi-hour lane nobody has funded -- so the required gate stays short; and the full suite is a **required** check on Linux, macOS and Windows rather than a best-effort leg, with lane promotion tracked in one machine-checked ledger instead of duplicated prose. Six issues now carry this feature's scope: a timeout ratchet (#374), a fixture-size policy plus the checkpoint-chain long-run capability (#378, redirected), the platform-promotion ledger and coverage-ratchet arming -- not the per-platform edits themselves (#406, redirected), the two remaining Wayland placeholders (#411), and two adopted display-lane-hardening tasks (#162, #91).

## Intended Audience & Impact

- **Six capstones** (`serves_capstones` below) whose acceptance runs are measured in hours. *Mirror state, read from each capstone's own machine block: #296, #300, #301 and #309 each name 317 in `requires_features`; #306's `requires_features` reads `[369]` and does not name this feature; #295 is closed as `not_planned` and has no body in the current corpus. So four of these six are confirmed from both sides and two need adjudication before the count can be relied on. `serves_capstones` is left as filed here, because dropping a capstone is that capstone's decision and not this feature's to make.* Today they have nowhere to run: a boot-scale run does not fit the required gate and there is no scheduled lane that hosts anything but the GUI leg. This feature's answer is no longer "give it a lane" but "make it segmentable" -- see Proposed disposition.
- **Anyone claiming cross-platform behaviour.** Two of the three platform lanes are advisory at `2d0ca9d`, so a cross-platform determinism claim currently rests on one platform's evidence plus two lanes that cannot fail the build.
- **Every contributor.** A wedged job today runs to the hosted ceiling. After this feature it is bounded by a number a reviewer can see in the workflow file.

## Status & Dependency Graph
