candidates.body:
Closes #50.

`!` negates a bool, at the unary level unary `-` already occupies:

```
!a:bool
!!a:bool
!(a:bool || b:bool)
!names:list<string>.contains:bool(needle:string)
```

It binds tighter than every binary operator and looser than the postfix dot, so `!a:bool && b:bool` is
`(!a:bool) && b:bool`, and a call is negated whole — which is the composition `x === false` couldn't express, since a
call can't sit on the left of a comparison in every position.

### The unary level gets a base class

Two unary operators are one more than `Precedence` could keep honest by naming concrete classes, so `Negative` and
`Not` share a `UnaryOperator` base that mirrors `BinaryOperator`: it carries the operand, the location the operator
starts at, and the token that fixes its spelling, and it prints through `Precedence`, so a subclass can't spell itself
differently than the lexer reads it. `Precedence::of()` names the base class instead of `Negative`, and
`parenthesize()` lost its last caller outside `Precedence`, so it's private now.

### `!` in the tokenizer

`!` no longer commits to `!==` on sight. One `=` after the bang still does — nothing that can follow a negation starts
with one — so `a:int != 1` is still reported as the `!==` it was reaching for. A bang with no `=` after it is the
negation operator, so a misplaced one is now an unexpected `!` rather than an unfinished `!==`:

| Input | Before | After |
|-------|--------|-------|
| `a:int != 1` | `Expected !==, got !=` | unchanged |
| `a:int ! 1` | `Expected !==, got !` | `Unexpected !` |
| `a:int !` | `Expected !==, got !` | `Unexpected !` |

### Type errors

The operand rule is the one `&&` and `||` follow, with the single operand `!` has to point at: `!foo:int` is
`The operand of ! must be boolean, got int`, underlining the operand alone. The shared check in `Expr` now takes how
the operand is named rather than an operator and a side; the `&&`/`||` messages are unchanged.

Nothing is folded, unlike a negated number literal: `!true` stays a negation of the literal `true`, because `false` is
a different expression that happens to evaluate the same.

### Checks

All green. One note on the BC check: `__toString()` and `equals()` are *not* final on `UnaryOperator`, unlike their
`BinaryOperator` counterparts. `Negative` published both non-final before there was a base class to move them to, and
Roave reports finalizing them as a break. It costs nothing to leave them open — every operator here is a final class,
so nothing can override them — and the class comment says so.

candidates.body:
Closes #51.

`-` was the only arithmetic operator; `+`, `*`, `/` and `%` were syntax errors, which made ratios, totals and "every nth" rules impossible to write.

## The operators

`+` and `*` are total operators exactly like `-`: both operands must be of the same numeric type, and the result is that type (new `Add` and `Multiply` nodes on the `Subtract` template).

`/` and `%` take the same operands but return an **`Option` of the operand type**: `int / int` is an `Option<int>`, and a zero divisor (including float `-0.0`) evaluates to `none` rather than throwing — the same shape `head` gives an empty list, consumed with the same `isSome`/`unwrap` idiom:

```
(a:int / b:int).unwrap:int()
(i:int % 3).unwrap:int() === 0
```

This keeps division total without a new runtime failure mode: every `EvaluationError` today means "the host lied at a boundary", never "the math went wrong", and that stays true. The alternatives considered — a `nonzero<T>` refinement type, a hybrid where literal divisors stay plain, a runtime error — lost out because refinements would leak subtype-awareness into every operator's type check, while the option is machinery the language already has.

Consequences, pinned by tests:

- An `int` quotient is `intdiv()`, truncated toward zero: `7 / 2` is `some(3)`, `-7 / 2` is `some(-3)`.
- A `float` remainder is `fmod()`, with the divisor checked first so its NAN-on-zero quirk can't get out. Remainders take the dividend's sign, for floats just like for ints.
- A quotient doesn't chain into further arithmetic or comparison without an `unwrap`: `a:int / b:int / c:int` and `a:int / b:int === 3` are type errors.
- `x / 0` is deliberately **not** a parse error: under option semantics it's a well-typed constant `none`, and the author already had to write the none-handling path.

## Precedence

`*`, `/` and `%` share a new `Multiplicative` level between `Additive` and `Unary`; `+` joins binary `-` on `Additive`. Levels are left-associative across their operators, so `a - b + c` is `(a - b) + c` and `a * b / c` is `(a * b) / c`. The cascade is now:

```
expression → or → and → comparison → additive → multiplicative → unary → postfix → primary
```

`Subtract` prints its right operand at the `Multiplicative` slot now (that's what the parser reads there), so `a - b * c` and `a - (b + c)` both round-trip; the `Precedence` levels were renumbered to make room, which is invisible outside the enum (`@internal`).

## Not in this PR

A true ratio from two ints (`a / b > 0.5`) is still inexpressible: it needs an int→float conversion built-in, which doesn't exist yet. That's the known follow-up if someone needs it.

## Verification

Full `composer check` is green: require-checker, cs-fixer, Psalm (level 1, strict binary operands), PHPStan (level max), 817 tests, and Infection at 100% MSI. One first-run escapee — removing `Modulo` from the `Multiplicative` arm of `Precedence::of()` — exposed a missing round-trip pin for `(a:int % b:int).unwrap:int()`, now added.

Split from #62.

`Peekable` held nothing but the generator and the last item consumed, so it could only ever see one item ahead and could never go back. Speculative parsing needs both.

Items are now buffered as they are pulled, with a cursor indexing into them: `peek($ahead)` looks past the next item without moving the cursor, `snapshot()` records where it is, and `restore()` puts it back. Nothing is pulled from the generator twice.

Two fixes fall out of the same rewrite:

- **The generator is only advanced once an item is actually asked for.** The tokenizer therefore scans the token that was peeked and not the text after it, so a mistake further right can't throw before the parser has reported the one it already found. `1 2 €` now blames the trailing `2` rather than the `€`.
- **A generator that throws is finished for good**, so the item it failed on will never arrive. Reporting that as end of input would turn a broken stream into a complete one, and `parseComplete()` would accept input it never managed to read. The failure is kept and raised again.

`snapshot()`/`restore()` land unused — nothing calls them until the `<`-vs-generic speculation in the last slice. `PeekableTest` covers them directly, so infection is at 100% MSI on the changed lines.

candidates.body:
Fixes #44.

## The bug

`&&` and `||` had the same precedence and were right-associative, so `a && b || c` parsed as `a && (b || c)` and silently returned the wrong result. Both operators parsed their right-hand side with the full `parseExpression()`, so whichever operator came first greedily swallowed everything to its right.

## The fix

`parseExpression()` now delegates to `parseOr()`, which parses its operands with `parseAnd()`, which parses its operands with the existing `parseExpressionUntilLogical()` (comparisons, arithmetic, calls, literals). The `&&`/`||` branch is gone from `parseLazy()` — the two new levels own those tokens now. Both levels loop instead of recursing, so `&&` and `||` are left-associative.

The bool-type checks on the operands moved into a shared `assertBooleanOperand()` helper; error messages and their source locations are unchanged.

Resulting precedence, tightest to loosest: `-`, then `===` and `>`, then `&&`, then `||`. Documented in the README, along with the note that grouping parentheses (#48) still don't exist, so the precedence can't be overridden.

## Tests

- Six end-to-end evaluation cases under `tests/unit/cases/precedence/`, including the exact reproduction from the issue (`a && b || c` with `a=false, b=false, c=true` → `true`).
- Four structural cases in `ExpressionParserTest` pinning the parse tree for `a && b || c`, `a || b && c`, and left-associative `&&`/`||` chains.
- Type-error message and location assertions for `&&` operands, which previously only existed for `||`.

Reverting just the parser change fails 5 of the new tests (2 precedence, 3 associativity). Mutation coverage of the changed lines is 100% MSI (14/14 mutants killed).

## Heads-up on CI

PHPStan currently reports 3 errors that are **pre-existing on `0.2.x`** and unrelated to this change: `Scope.php:225`, `Type.php:104`, and a `nullsafe.neverNull` in `ExpressionParser::parseParam()`. They surface because there's no `composer.lock` and CI runs `composer update`, which now resolves a newer PHPStan than the last green run used. Since PHPStan gates the Infection job, this branch's CI may be red for those reasons. Happy to fix them in a separate PR.

## Summary

Defines the public surface as **every `public` symbol not marked `@internal`**, the pre-1.0 rule that the **minor is the compatibility boundary**, the split between structural and behavioral breaks, how the check runs, and how the version is chosen and recorded.

`Delimiters` and `TypeParser` carried `@psalm-internal` but **not** `@internal`, so Roave (which only recognizes `@internal`) treated them as public API. The `Backward Compatibility` job runs Roave as:
- **informational** on `master` and feature branches — during a pre-release minor cycle the trunk intentionally accumulates the next version's breaks, so a reported break there is expected;
- **blocking** on maintenance branches (`*.x`, e.g. `0.3.x`), which promise compatibility.

Implemented via `continue-on-error: ${{ !endsWith(github.base_ref, '.x') }}`.

PHPUnit (1030 tests), PHP CS Fixer, PHPStan, and Psalm all pass locally. Infection is unaffected — the only `src` changes are docblock lines (no mutations), and the new test lives in `tests/`. Roave itself only runs in CI.

candidates.body:
Closes #92. Scoped for the **0.3.0 breaking release**.

## Problem

The fluent builder on `Expression` is our most-used public `@api` surface, but nine of its fifteen combinators declared a **class-level `@internal`** node as their return type while the other six returned `self`. So the surface both leaked internal symbols *and* contradicted itself — `eq` returned `Eq` but its sibling `neq` returned `self`; `gt` returned `Gt` but `lt`/`gte`/`lte` returned `self`.

Separately, `Eq` and `Gt` were BC shims: `@internal final` subclasses of `Comparison` that added nothing but a fixed constructor. They only still existed because `Expression::eq()`/`gt()` named them as return types before `Comparison` existed.

## Changes

- **All fifteen `Expression` builder combinators now return `self`.** The rationale that was spelled out on `not()`'s docblock is now the class-level rule, so it moved to the class docblock and the per-method note is gone.
- **`Expr::eq()`/`gt()` return `Comparison`** and construct through the shared `comparison()` helper.
- **`Eq` and `Gt` are removed**; they fold into `Comparison`, which is now `final` (all six operators are plain instances of it). `Comparison::equals()` already matches on `self`, so a former `Eq`/`Gt` value and a plain `Comparison` compare equal — behavior is preserved.
- Docblocks on `Comparison` and `BinaryOperator` updated to drop the `Eq`/`Gt` references and the "four of six" framing.
- One test's data-provider name-builder discriminated closures from expressions with `is_callable()`, which only worked because the builders returned *final concrete* nodes. With `self` (abstract `Expression`, possibly-callable via a hypothetical `__invoke` subclass) PHPStan widened `$expr()` to `mixed`. Reordered it to check `instanceof Expression` first, mirroring the consuming test method.
- Added an UPGRADING note for the break.

## BC impact

Structural break — return-type narrowing on public methods plus two class removals. The Roave checker will flag it. Correct for a `0.MINOR` bump; frozen after 1.0.0, at which point we'd be stuck publishing `Eq`/`Add`/… as permanent public types.

## Checks

`cs-check`, `psalm`, `phpstan`, `check-deps`, `phpunit` (1152 tests), and `infection` on changed lines (100% MSI) all pass locally.

candidates.body:
Closes #59.

`TypeParser::parse()` returned `TypeNode|ParsedToken|null`, which left every call site to work out whether a type had actually been read and to word its own complaint if not. Six of the seven callers did that, in six wordings, and each new place a type can appear grew another copy — that was the root cause behind the `E2eCase` finding in #58.

A type is required everywhere one may appear, so this settles it in `parse()`: return `TypeNode`, throw `SyntaxError` otherwise.

The one caller that genuinely had to ask whether a type was next is `parseTypeList()`, which now takes the bracket it ends at (`CloseAngle` or `CloseParen`) and peeks for it instead of reading the answer off a failed parse. Running out of input ends the list too, so the caller's `expect($close)` still gets to name the bracket that's missing rather than this asking for another element.

That drops the decode-and-throw blocks from `parseString()`, `parseDeclarations()`, `parseFunction()`, `parseStruct()` and both `ExpressionParser` sites. The duplicated end-of-input span computation in `expect()` moved into a shared `endOfInput()` helper, which `parse()` reuses and which handles "nothing was ever read" directly instead of asserting it away.

## Error messages

The issue asked which wording we actually want. This collapses the five bespoke ones into `expect()`'s existing convention, `Expected type, got X` / `Expected type, got end of input`:

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| `Expected return type, got .` | `Expected type, got .` |
| `Expected a type for Foo, got ->` | `Expected type, got ->` |
| `Expected type after colon, got X` | `Expected type, got X` |
| `Expected type, got end of string` | `Expected type, got end of input` |
| `Invalid type ""` | `Expected type, got end of input` |

The context those wordings carried ("return type", "for Foo") is what the `Span` on the error is for, and it points at the offending token in every case. The span for the empty-string case is unchanged at 1:1.

One genuine behavior change, the one the issue predicted: inside an argument list, a token that can't start a type is now blamed as the element it isn't rather than as a missing bracket. `list<int 42>` reports `Expected type, got 42` instead of `Expected >, got 42`. Added test cases pinning this for both `<...>` and `fn(...)`.

## Notes for review

- **The rewind path is unaffected.** `tryTypeArguments()` catches `SyntaxError`, so `a:Foo < b:int` still falls back to reading the `<` as a less-than: `parseTypeList()` now throws where it previously broke out of the loop, and the existing catch swallows it identically.
- **No new BC break.** `parse()` is public on a `final` class, and narrowing `TypeNode|ParsedToken|null` to `TypeNode` is covariant. `roave-backward-compatibility-check` from `0.2.4` gives byte-identical output against this commit and against the base (one pre-existing `SKIPPED` on `Declarations.php`).
- Only the six predicted message assertions needed updating; no other test changed behavior.

Green locally: 774 tests, Psalm, PHPStan, php-cs-fixer, composer-require-checker, and 100% MSI (25/25 mutants killed) on the changed lines.

candidates.body:
Closes #48.

`(` was only recognized as the start of a call's argument list, so sub-expressions couldn't be grouped and precedence couldn't be overridden. Some boolean expressions had no valid spelling at all — e.g. `(a && b) || c`.

## Parsing

`(...)` is now handled at the tightest level of the cascade (`parsePrimary`): it consumes the parens and re-enters via `parseExpression()`, so a group is a whole expression whatever surrounds it. **Grouping adds no AST node** — the tree is the one the operators would have built anyway. The tokenizer already emitted `(`/`)`, so it was unchanged.

## Round-tripping `__toString`

The parser can now build trees whose grouping overrides the default precedence (e.g. `a && (b || c)` → `And(a, Or(b, c))`). The old flat `__toString` would have printed that as `a && b || c`, which re-parses to a *different* tree. To keep `__toString` a faithful serialization, the new internal `Precedence` helper mirrors the parser cascade, and each operator wraps an operand in parentheses **exactly when it binds looser than its slot allows**:

- Required parens are reproduced: `a:bool && (b:bool || c:bool)`, `a:int - (b:int - c:int)`, `(-a:int).abs:int()`
- Redundant parens are dropped: `(a:int - b:int) - c:int` → `a:int - b:int - c:int`
- `parse(str(e))` equals `e` for every grouped tree

## Tests

- `parseCases`: one canonical case per cascade level forced inside a looser one (asserts both the parse and the printed form)
- `nonCanonicalParseCases`: redundant-paren inputs that get dropped, including the issue's `(a:int - 1) - 2`
- Syntax errors + two location assertions: `()`, unclosed, stray `)`, comma inside parens
- Three end-to-end evaluation cases proving grouping changes the *result* (e.g. `a && (b || c)` evaluates to `false` where the default grouping gives `true`)

README's "no grouping parentheses yet" is replaced with a **Grouping** section.

Infection passes at 100% MSI / 100% mutation coverage on the changed lines.

candidates.body:
Closes #45.

### The bug is already fixed

Every reproduction in #45 parses and evaluates today. Parsing expressions as a precedence cascade (ef9db06, #56) fixed it as a side effect: `parseArg()`, `parseListLiteral()` and `parseStructField()` went from a single `parseLazy(null)` pass to `parseExpression()`, which is exactly the fix the issue prescribes. Nothing under `src/` changes here.

### What was missing

That commit witnessed those positions with `-` alone, and `-` was never what the issue was about — it reports calls, field access, and comparison/logical operators.

The gap was real, not hypothetical: downgrading all three positions to `parseAdditive()` — which still takes the `-` of the existing cases and the `.` of a postfix, but no `===` and no `||` — leaves the entire pre-existing suite green. Nothing pinned how far the cascade reaches into those positions, so a later parser change could have put the reported bug back with no test complaining.

### What this adds

One expression that spans the whole cascade, nested in each of the three positions:

```
o:{ n: string }.n === s:string.substr:string(0, 1) || b:bool
```

`||` is the cascade's loosest level, and the postfix `.` of a field access and of a call its tightest, so a position that parses it has to run every level in between. That says more than a case per operator would, and covers what the issue reports in one go. The list and struct cases put a second element behind it, because the operators in it must not swallow the comma that ends it.

Three parse cases pin the AST, three end-to-end cases pin evaluation. Each is load-bearing and position-specific: downgrading one position's parser fails exactly that position's two tests and no others, and under the `parseAdditive()` downgrade above only these six fail.

The README claimed only that *operators* were allowed in those positions, and showed it with `-` alone; it now says calls and field access are too.

### Verification

`composer check` is green: php-cs-fixer, Psalm, PHPStan, 603 PHPUnit tests, and Infection at 100% MSI / 100% covered MSI.

candidates.body:
Closes #49. Split from #62.

Rebased onto `0.2.x` now that #64, #66, #67 and #68 have merged — the diff below is this slice alone.

The language had `===` and `>` and nothing else, so half the comparisons had to be spelled around: `a >= b` as `a > b || a === b`, and inequality as a negation the language has no operator for at all.

## Tokenizing

`!==` joins `===` and `&&` in `exact()`: once the `!` is there the whole sequence is required, so `!=` is an error naming the operator it fell short of.

`<` and `>` now each stand for two things, so they move out of the single-character match into `angle()`: bare they are a generic's angle brackets, followed by `=` they are `<=` and `>=`. The pair reading wins **with one exception** — two `=` after the angle mean a `===` follows, as in `foo:list<int>===bar`, so the angle stays bare rather than stealing the first `=` and leaving a `==` that is no token at all. That one-character lookahead is what `peek(1)` (#64) is for.

## Parsing `<`

`a:int < b:int` is ambiguous with a generic's argument list, and the tokenizer can't settle it — the `<` after `int` looks the same either way. `TypeParser` now decides it by what precedes the `<`:

- **A constructor that takes type arguments** (`list`, `map`, `Option`, `Some`) is committed. The `<` can only open its argument list, so an error inside is a genuine error, reported where it happens.
- **Any other name** might be an operand, so `tryTypeArguments()` reads a list speculatively and hands the `<` back if what follows isn't one. This is what `snapshot()`/`restore()` (#64) are for. A `SyntaxError` raised along the way isn't reported: it only means these tokens aren't a type argument list either.

A closed list after a name that takes none (`int<string>`, `Foo<int>`) is still read as a type on purpose, so the resolver rejects it by name (#66) rather than the parser silently re-reading the `<` as less-than.

Speculation is why a failed pull has to stay failed: the `$` in `[a:int < b, c $]` is tokenized while trying a reading that is then abandoned, and it is still the mistake once the `<` has been re-read.

## The operators

`parseComparison()` reads all six through one match. They stay non-associative, so a chain of any of them is a syntax error rather than a comparison against the bool the first one produced.

The four new ones need no node of their own: each is a `Comparison` (#68) holding its `ComparisonOperator`. `!==` is exactly the negation of `===`, sharing `ValueEquality` rather than restating deep structural equality. `Expr` and `Expression` gain `neq`/`lt`/`gte`/`lte` to match the existing `eq`/`gt`.

Infection passes at 100% MSI / 100% covered MSI on the changed lines (90 mutants).

candidates.body:
Type variables in function signatures, decided per call site. Unblocks #47.

```
nums:list<int>.map(|n| n:int > 2)     // list<bool>, nothing spelled out
names:list<string>.head()             // Option<string>
nums:list<int>.contains("foo")        // error: Argument 1 of contains must be of type int, got string
```

## What's in it

**Syntax.** A function type may bind type variables in front of its parameter list: `fn<T, U>(list<T>, fn(T) -> U) -> list<U>`. A binder is the whole of a variable's scope, so a variable is a type anywhere below the `fn` that binds it, and a name no binder declares is still an alias or an error — a misspelled alias doesn't quietly become a variable. In PHP a variable is `Type::var('T')`.

**Inference** (`Type::instantiate()`). One-way and structural. Parameters are walked receiver first and a variable keeps the **first** type that lands on it, with no variance tracking. That ordering is the whole trick: a lambda's parameters are typed `any` and would decide nothing useful, but the receiver has already decided by the time one is looked at. A variable no operand reaches becomes `any` rather than an error.

Nothing in instantiation reports a mistake. The substituted signature is what `Expr::call()`'s existing receiver and argument checks run against, so error messages still point at the expression that's wrong — and they got sharper for free: `x:int.contains(42)` now says `must be called on an expression of type list<int>` instead of `list<any>`.

**All twelve built-ins are declared now.** Five of them (`filter`, `map`, `count`, `some`, `take`) rode the escape hatch for undeclared functions purely because there was no way to write "a list of whatever it is". The ones that *were* declared got tighter alongside them — `contains` took an `any` needle and now takes one of the list's own element type.

## ⚠️ Breaking

`filter` and `map` no longer accept a `map<K, V>` receiver. They only ever did because they were undeclared — every sibling (`count`, `contains`, `some`, `take`, `unique`) already rejected one — and a signature that preserves map keys isn't expressible. Both are declared over `list<T>` now, and `BuiltinFunctions::filter()` lost its key-preserving branch to match.

## Tests

The generics tests are fixtures under `tests/unit/cases/generics/` (39 of them), not a PHP test class. That needed the harness to grow sections:

- `-- Expression type --` — the expression's static type, printed; combinable with `-- Output --`
- `-- Syntax error --` / `-- Type error --` — the expected message; *which* section you use pins the class
- `-- Functions --` — call signatures, same `Name: <type>` shape as `-- Types --`
- `-- Note --` — prose, asserts nothing

`-- Output --` is now optional, and an unknown section name is an error rather than a case that quietly asserts nothing.

Infection was useful here beyond coverage: three escaped mutants in `bind()`/`instantiate()` were *equivalent* mutants, which was the metric pointing out that `$arguments[$index] ?? null` spells a hole a list can never have. Those loops now slice to the common length and intersect on field keys, so the impossible case isn't written down at all. The fourth was genuinely untested and got two fixtures.

## README

Documents the syntax and adds a Signature column to the built-in table. `BuiltinFunctionsTest` parses each cell back into a `Type` and compares it to the declared one, so the table can't drift. Examples dropped their now-redundant inline return types.

## Notes for review

- **Scope:** generic *function signatures* only. No generic type aliases (`Bag<T>`) in this pass.
- `roave-backward-compatibility-check` could not run locally — it refuses to run in a git worktree. CI is the first real check on it. The public surface only gains methods on a `final` class, so I don't expect a finding.
- Still open, and deliberately untouched: `Type::__toString()` prints `func(a, b): r` while the parser reads `fn(a, b) -> r`, so a function type doesn't round-trip. It predates this branch but is more visible now that signatures appear in error messages and in the README. Worth its own issue; fixing it here would churn every error-message assertion.

candidates.body:
Makes `composer check` green again on the current PHPStan/Psalm/ComposerRequireChecker releases. Both errors PHPStan reported turned out to be real problems rather than analyzer noise.

## Summary

- **`Peekable::next()` was not declared impure** — PHPStan carried an earlier `peek()`'s null narrowing across it and called a nullsafe operator redundant; taking its advice would have introduced a null dereference.
- **`Type::fromValue()` leaked non-string field names into structs** — `get_object_vars()` keys are not necessarily strings, producing struct fields the language cannot express.
- **`check-deps` downloaded the latest CRC phar** — which since 4.21.0 requires PHP >= 8.4 and fataled the PHP 8.3 CI jobs before running any check.

## `Peekable::next()` was not declared impure

`next()` advances the underlying generator, but PHPStan assumed it was side effect free. It therefore carried the "not null" narrowing of an earlier `peek()` across the `next()` call and flagged the nullsafe operator in `parseParam()` as redundant:

> Using nullsafe property access on non-nullable type ParsedToken. Use -> instead.

Following that advice would have introduced a null dereference on trailing input such as `|foo`, because after `next()` the next `peek()` can legitimately return `null` at end of input. Declaring `next()` impure states a true fact about the method and makes the narrowing correctly invalidate.

## `Type::fromValue()` leaked non-string field names into structs

`fromValue()` built struct fields straight from `get_object_vars()`, whose keys are *not* necessarily strings. PHP normalizes numeric property names to integer array keys, so `json_decode('{"1": "a"}')` yields an int key, which then became a struct field:

```php
Type::fromValue(json_decode('{"1": "a", "foo": "b"}'));
// before: { 1: string, foo: string }
// after:  { foo: string }
```

Those names are not valid identifiers, so they can be neither declared in a struct type (`{ 1: string }` → *Expected field name, got 1*) nor accessed in an expression (`s.1` → *Expected function name, got 1*). They are therefore dropped instead of being passed off as fields. A PHP array cannot hold `"1"` as a string key at all, which means the documented `array<string, Type>` shape of `Type::$fields` was not merely imprecise, it was unsatisfiable — this change makes it true rather than relaxing it.

## Composer Require Checker ran against the wrong PHP version

`check-deps` downloaded the phar from `releases/latest`, a URL with no notion of which PHP version the job runs on. ComposerRequireChecker dropped PHP 8.3 support in 4.21.0 (4.21+ require `~8.4.0 || ~8.5.0`), so both PHP 8.3 jobs fataled on startup:

> Your Composer dependencies require a PHP version ">= 8.4.0". You are running 8.3.32.

`maglnet/composer-require-checker` is already a dev dependency, so the installed binary is used instead. Composer resolves it against the PHP version in use, so each job gets a compatible release automatically rather than whatever happens to be newest — no hand-pinned version to maintain. Verified across the matrix: 8.3 and 8.4 resolve 4.20.0, both `--prefer-lowest` jobs resolve 4.16.0, and all four run clean.

## Backward compatibility

No public type is widened. `Type::struct()` and the public readonly `Type::$fields` keep their exact `array<string, Type>` signature; the fix is at the boundary that violated it. `roave-backward-compatibility-check` against `0.2.x` reports no new findings (the single `[BC] SKIPPED: Unable to compile initializer in class Declarations` it prints also appears when comparing `0.2.x` against itself, so it is a pre-existing tool limitation).

The only behavior change is the edge case above: an object with numeric property names no longer contributes them as struct fields. Field access, `assert()`, and subtype checks are unaffected for anything the language can express.

`Scope::printValue()` and the `Shape` alias do widen to `array<array-key, mixed>`, since a debug dump should show a numerically-named property rather than hide it. Both are private/`@internal` and reachable from no public signature.

## Verification

`composer check` passes: composer-require-checker, PHP-CS-Fixer, Psalm, PHPStan (level max), 542 tests, and Infection at 100% MSI with no escaped mutants. CI is green on all 25 jobs.

## What landed

### `cargo xtask check-*` (7 new commands)

```
cargo xtask check-file-policy [--mode <advisory|blocking-allowlist>]
cargo xtask check-generated [--mode ...]
cargo xtask check-executable-files [--mode ...]
cargo xtask check-workflows [--mode ...]
cargo xtask check-dependency-surfaces [--mode ...]
cargo xtask check-process-policy [--mode ...]
cargo xtask check-network-policy [--mode ...]
```

### Implementation per checker

| Checker | What it does |
|---|---|
| `check-file-policy` | Glob-match every non-Rust file (via `git ls-files`) against `non-rust-allowlist.toml`; flag broad globs without `broad_glob_reason` |
| `check-generated` | Parse `.gitattributes` for `linguist-generated=true` entries; cross-check against `generated-allowlist.toml` (drift in both directions) |
| `check-executable-files` | `git ls-files --stage`; check files with mode `100755` against `executable-allowlist.toml` (drift in both directions) |
| `check-workflows` | For each `.github/workflows/*.yml`: verify allowlist entry exists; cross-check `uses:` lines against the entry's `external_actions` |
| `check-dependency-surfaces` | For each entry's `path` / `glob`: verify it matches at least one tracked file |
| `check-process-policy` | v1: validate required ledger fields per entry (`id`, `binary`, `argv_shape`, `network_reach`, `owner`, `reason`, `created`) |
| `check-network-policy` | v1: validate required ledger fields per entry (`id`, `destination`, `auth_required`, `lane`, `owner`, `reason`, `created`) |

`check-process-policy` and `check-network-policy` defer source scanning (looking up actual `Command::new` / `reqwest` call sites) to a follow-up release. v1 is ledger-validation only.

|---|---|

| `policy/executable-allowlist.toml` | − 2 stale entries removed: `scripts/release-install-smoke.ps1` and `scripts/demo-review-rescue.ps1` are tracked at mode `100644` (not executable), and PowerShell is invoked as `pwsh script.ps1` anyway — they remain covered by `non-rust-allowlist.toml`'s `scripts/*.ps1` glob |
| `policy/network-allowlist.toml` | + `owner` field added to 8 entries that were missing it (schema requires `owner` per `docs/POLICY_ALLOWLISTS.md`) |

### Reviewer spot-check map (test → concern)

| Concern | Covering test |
|---|---|
| Process-policy required-field validation (success path) | `process_policy_validates_required_fields` |
| Process-policy required-field validation (missing-field detection) | `process_policy_finds_missing_required_fields` |
| Network-policy required-field validation (success path) | `network_policy_validates_required_fields` |
| Generated drift detection (.gitattributes ↔ allowlist mismatch) | `generated_finds_drift_between_gitattributes_and_allow` |
| Generated alignment (success path) | `generated_passes_when_aligned` |
| YAML `uses:` extraction (list-marker prefix + inline comment + edge cases) | `extract_uses_strips_inline_comments` |
| Mode dispatch (advisory vs blocking-allowlist) | covered by every test that asserts pass/fail behavior across both modes |

- ❌ Wiring any checker into a CI workflow (no enforcement on PRs in v0.5.0; opt-in via direct `cargo xtask check-*` invocation only)

## Summary

Massive workspace decomposition extracting **145 new microcrates** from the shiplog monolith, along with new ingest adapters, CI workflows, testing infrastructure, and documentation. This follows the project's core architectural principle of preferring new orthogonal microcrates over enlarging existing ones.

### Highlights

- **Redaction subsystem decomposition (6 crates):** Extracted `shiplog-alias`, `shiplog-redaction-policy`, `shiplog-redaction-profile`, `shiplog-redaction-projector`, `shiplog-redaction-repo`, and `shiplog-sanitize` from the monolithic `shiplog-redact` crate for finer-grained dependency control.
- **Cache subsystem decomposition (7 crates):** Extracted `shiplog-cache-2q`, `shiplog-cache-arc`, `shiplog-cache-expiry`, `shiplog-cache-key`, `shiplog-cache-lru`, `shiplog-cache-stats`, and `shiplog-cache-ttl` from `shiplog-cache`.
- **Team subsystem decomposition (4 crates):** Split `shiplog-team` into `shiplog-team-core`, `shiplog-team-aggregate`, `shiplog-team-render`, keeping the original as a facade.
- **New ingest adapters (4 crates):** Added `shiplog-ingest-git` (local git repos), `shiplog-ingest-linear` (Linear issues), `shiplog-ingest-gitlab`, and `shiplog-ingest-jira` scaffolding.
- **Data structure microcrates (18 crates):** Foundation-tier data structures (`shiplog-bloom`, `shiplog-bst`, `shiplog-btree`, `shiplog-heap`, `shiplog-ring`, `shiplog-skiplist`, `shiplog-trie`, etc.) for internal use.
- **Infrastructure/utility microcrates (~101 crates):** General-purpose utilities following the single-responsibility principle: `shiplog-sync`, `shiplog-time`, `shiplog-retry`, `shiplog-metrics`, `shiplog-throttler`, `shiplog-buffer`, `shiplog-channel`, `shiplog-auth`, and many more.
- **Feature scaffolding (5 crates):** Future feature entry points: `shiplog-tui`, `shiplog-web`, `shiplog-plugin`, `shiplog-cron`, `shiplog-workflow`.

### CI & Testing

- Added **6 new GitHub Actions workflows**: BDD testing, fuzzing, mutation testing, property testing, release, and security scanning.
- Enhanced `cargo-mutants.toml` configuration with keepalive for long-running mutations.
- Expanded BDD test infrastructure with merge, team, and microcrate contract scenarios.
- Comprehensive testing strategy plans in `plans/`.

### Documentation

- Added `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `HANDOFF.md`, `ROADMAP.md`, and `RELEASE_HANDOFF_0.2.1.md`.
- Added README files for individual crates.
- Updated `CLAUDE.md` and `GEMINI.md` with current architecture.

### Other Changes

- Updated workspace `Cargo.toml` and `Cargo.lock` for all new dependencies.
- Added `.cargo/config.toml` for workspace configuration.
- Centralized artifact paths via `shiplog-output-layout`.
- Fixed clippy `derivable_impls` lint in `shiplog-redaction-profile`.

## Stats

- **33 commits** on `feature/microcrate-extraction-v2`
- **614 files changed**, ~77,500 insertions, ~1,250 deletions
- **145 new crates** added to the workspace
- All tests passing, formatting clean, clippy clean

- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check` clean

## Release v0.1.0

This PR prepares the shiplog project for its v0.1.0 release, introducing the SQLite cache integration and hardening the workspace for production use.

### 🚀 New Features

#### Local SQLite Cache (`shiplog-cache`)
- **Durable caching** for GitHub API responses to reduce API calls and speed up repeated runs
- **TTL-based expiration** (default 24 hours) with configurable per-entry TTL
- **Cache key builder** for GitHub endpoints (`CacheKey::pr_details()`, `CacheKey::pr_reviews()`)
- **In-memory cache support** for testing environments
- **Cache statistics and cleanup utilities** (`stats()`, `cleanup_expired()`)

#### GitHub Ingestor Cache Integration
- `GithubIngestor::with_cache()` - Enable file-based SQLite caching
- `GithubIngestor::with_in_memory_cache()` - Enable in-memory caching for tests
- **Automatic cache lookup** before API calls for PR details and reviews
- **Transparent cache storage** after fetches with automatic serialization

### 🔧 Technical Improvements

#### Serde Derive Hardening
- Fixed serde import issues using fully-qualified derives (`serde::Serialize`, `serde::Deserialize`)
- Eliminated "unused import" warnings in test modules
- Proper `Serialize` derives on all cached DTOs (`PullRequestDetails`, `PullRequestReview`, etc.)

#### Warning Cleanup
- Fixed doc comment on proptest macro (converted to regular comment)
- **Zero compiler warnings** across entire workspace
- Clean `cargo clippy --workspace` run

#### ApiCache Enhancements
- Added `Clone` implementation for `GithubIngestor` derive compatibility
- Added `Debug` derive for better debugging experience

### 📋 Changelog

See [CHANGELOG.md](./CHANGELOG.md) for detailed version history:
- **v0.0.1**: Initial project structure
- **v0.1.0**: All features including caching, redaction, workstreams, and rendering

┌─────────────────┐     ┌──────────────┐     ┌─────────────────┐

## Summary

Documents-only roadmap for shiplog **0.5.0** ("Operational Review Rescue + Rust 1.95 quality floor + policy/CI economics foundation"). No Cargo, toolchain, workflow, or Rust changes. This is **PR #140** of an 18-PR ladder (#140–#157 across 9 phases); subsequent PRs land in independent slices.

This release bundles three things that travel together:

1. The operational hardening lane already merged after v0.4.0 (PRs #125–#139).
2. An MSRV bump from Rust **1.92 → 1.95** (slipped from v0.4.0).
3. A first cut of policy ledgers, a thin Rust-native `xtask` runner, an advisory LEM-budgeted CI lane plan, and `ripr` advisory routing. Hard CI budget enforcement is a follow-up release decision, not v0.5.0.

## Files added

Policy doctrine:

- `docs/CLIPPY_POLICY.md` — Clippy lint ledger model, suppression style (`#[expect]` not bare `#[allow]`), no test carveouts
- `docs/NO_PANIC_POLICY.md` — exact-identity (path + family + selector_kind + selector_callee + snippet + count) no-new-debt baseline
- `docs/FILE_POLICY.md` — non-Rust + companion ledgers (generated, executable, dependency, workflow, process, network); shell-script-as-wrapper rule
- `docs/POLICY_ALLOWLISTS.md` — common schema (path / owner / reason / expiry) and per-ledger extension fields

CI economics:

- `docs/ci/rust-1.95-rollout.md` — master map: current vs target, existing workflow inventory, **tentative/advisory** lane assignments, 18-PR / 9-phase ladder, acceptance gates, per-PR operating contract, definition of done
- `docs/ci/cost-and-verification-policy.md` — verification economics doctrine, agentic-volume cost framing (~1,000 contributions/day, ~\$30k/mo at \$1/PR, OpenClaw ~\$20/commit comparison), operating rule (6 questions per lane), `ripr` and mutation economics
- `docs/ci/lem-budgeting.md` — Linux Equivalent Minutes cost unit, runner multipliers (ubuntu 1×, windows 2×, macos 10×, docker 6×, AI 4×), budget tiers, **stochastic budget rule** (proptest 16–64 cases per selected test; quick fuzz 30–90s on touched target only)
- `docs/ci/verification-ladder.md` — signal-vs-spend ladder per lane, where the rollout shifts spend, claim boundaries
- `docs/ci/test-evidence-lanes.md` — PR fast / PR-targeted / nightly / release lane assignments, **bounded vs broad stochastic** doctrine, `ripr` and mutation economics block, promotion paths

Updated:

- `CHANGELOG.md` — `[Unreleased]` populated with the rollout pointer set

## Doctrine encoded

- **Bounded stochastic on PR fast.** Property tests, fuzzing, and BDD scenarios are not inherently expensive. The cost driver is *unscoped* stochastic testing. The rollout keeps bounded forms (selected high-value invariants at 16–64 cases; touched-target quick fuzz at 30–90s; one or two BDD critical-flow smoke tests) on the PR fast lane and routes broad sweeps to PR-targeted (label / risk pack) and nightly.
- **\`ripr\` and mutation economics.** \`ripr\` advisory on every PR (~3–6 LEM) is the reason full mutation can defer off the default PR gate. Mutation calibrates ripr over time, not the other way around.
- **Operating rule.** Every CI lane must answer six questions before it can claim a default-PR slot.
- **Agentic-volume framing.** Verification must be *engineered*, not skipped. The goal is more proof per CI minute, not cheaper CI.

1. **Enhanced Coverage Workflow** — Upgraded `.github/workflows/coverage.yml` with:

   - Range specification (50–85%)
   - Flag-based grouping (`rust-core`)

   - GitHub Checks annotations disabled
   - Informational-only statuses (not blocking)

3. **README Badge** — Added Codecov badge immediately after CI badge

4. **Documentation** — Added `docs/ci/coverage.md` explaining:
   - What Codecov coverage measures (execution-surface evidence)
   - What it does not measure (manifest completeness, packet quality, redaction safety, etc.)
   - Workflow triggers and durable receipts
   - Claim boundaries

## CI economics

- Workflow impact: ~45 minutes on ubuntu-latest (optimized with larger target dir)
- Branch protection: Advisory only (not blocking)
- Failure mode: Coverage generation failure surfaces in CI, Codecov upload failure is non-blocking on PRs

- Rollback path: Disable workflow or remove from push triggers

Codecov coverage is **execution-surface evidence only**.

It does not prove:
- shiplog coverage-manifest completeness
- packet quality or review-readiness

## Summary

Implements Codecov integration for shiplog as a separate, non-blocking coverage workflow on Ubuntu using `cargo-llvm-cov` and `codecov/codecov-action@v5`.

## Changes

- **`.github/workflows/coverage.yml`**: New separate workflow that runs on push/PR to `main` and on manual trigger
  - Uses Rust 1.92 with `llvm-tools-preview`
  - Generates LCOV coverage with `cargo-llvm-cov`
  - Excludes `shiplog-testkit` from baseline to measure product code only
  - Uploads LCOV as a GitHub artifact (14-day retention)
  - Uploads to Codecov with `fail_ci_if_error: false` (non-blocking during baseline setup)
  - 30-minute timeout, 4 test threads, full features
  - Concurrency group prevents duplicate runs per ref

- **`codecov.yml`**: Conservative advisory configuration
  - Comments disabled to avoid review noise at initial rollout
  - Project coverage: auto target, 5% threshold, informational
  - Patch coverage: 70% target, 10% threshold, informational
  - Ignores: `shiplog-testkit`, `fuzz`, `examples`, `benches`, `target`
  - Precision: 2 decimals, round down

## Why This Design

- **Separate workflow**: Keeps normal CI clean and avoids doubling test cost across platforms
- **Ubuntu only**: Coverage is a source signal, not an OS portability check
- **Exclude shiplog-testkit**: Test carrier, not product coverage surface
- **Non-blocking**: Codecov failures don't block PRs while baseline matures
- **Artifact upload**: Preserves LCOV even if Codecov has outages
- **Informational thresholds**: Advisory signal until baseline stabilizes after 10–20 PRs

## Next Steps

After 10–20 normal PRs:
1. Review Codecov dashboard and coverage-lcov artifacts
2. Verify workflow runtime cost and patch coverage behavior
3. Tighten thresholds if baseline is stable (e.g., project → 2% informational, patch → 60% threshold 20%)
4. Later: consider mutation testing and property workflow integration

## Verification

- ✅ `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- ✅ `cargo check --workspace --all-features`
- ✅ Commit pushed to branch

---

## Summary

Adds the 13 human-readable CI operating-contract docs and 2 JSON Schemas for the artifacts the LEM PR plan (#146) and CI actuals collector (#148) will emit. This is **PR #142** of the v0.5.0 ladder (Phase 1 — machine-readable roadmap), pairing with the TOML ledgers landed in #141.

No Rust code, no workflow changes, no enforcement. The docs make every later implementation PR read from a declared contract instead of inventing policy in code.

## PR acceptance contract

- **Scope:** human CI operating-contract docs + JSON schemas for ci-plan/ci-actuals
- **Files expected:** \`docs/ci/*.md\` (13 files) + \`contracts/schemas/*.json\` (2 files)
- **Behavior change:** no
- **Advisory vs blocking:** none (docs + schemas only)
- **New artifacts:** 13 docs + 2 JSON Schemas (v1 stable contracts)
- **Validation commands:**
  - \`python -c "import json; [json.load(open(p)) for p in ['contracts/schemas/ci-plan.v1.schema.json','contracts/schemas/ci-actuals.v1.schema.json']]"\`
  - \`cargo fmt --all -- --check\`
  - \`cargo check --workspace --all-targets --locked\`
  - \`git diff --check\`
- **Rollback path:** \`git revert <merge-sha>\` — no enforcement to unwind, no Rust touched
- **Follow-up PR:** #143 (xtask runner that loads the policy ledgers); #146 (PR plan that emits \`ci-plan.json\` against the v1 schema); #148 (CI actuals collector that emits \`ci-actuals.json\` against the v1 schema)

## Files added

### CI operating contracts (\`docs/ci/\`)

| Doc | Purpose | Pairs with |
|---|---|---|
| \`ci-lane-map.md\` | Mechanical inventory: every workflow/job, intent, base LEM, evidence, duplicate_of, target lane, owner | \`policy/ci-lanes.toml\` |
| \`labels.md\` | 12 PR label semantics (spend authorization vs routing toggles) | \`policy/ci-budget.toml#labels\` |
| \`risk-packs.md\` | 12 named path-pattern → label/lane packs | \`policy/ci-risk-packs.toml\` |
| \`branch-protection.md\` | Rule: require summary checks, not matrix leaves, not advisory lanes | \`policy/ci-lanes.toml#blocking\` |
| \`required-check-migration.md\` | Sequenced migration to avoid GitHub pending-check deadlocks | branch-protection |
| \`skipped-by-policy.md\` | 7 definite skip categories — no silent skips | ci-actuals |
| \`bot-review-policy.md\` | Droid/Gemini/CodeRabbit are advisory; rate-limit non-blocking; bot ≠ code failure | \`policy/workflow-allowlist.toml\` droid entries |
| \`cache-policy.md\` | PRs restore caches, \`main\` saves canonical, matrix restore-only, release-specific keys | (PR #147 implements) |
| \`ci-plan-json.md\` | Forecast contract (paired with v1 schema) | \`ci-plan.v1.schema.json\` |
| \`ci-actuals.md\` | Actuals contract (paired with v1 schema) | \`ci-actuals.v1.schema.json\` |
| \`ripr.md\` | Oracle-gap detector operating doc; ripr/mutation economics | \`policy/ripr-suppressions.toml\` (PR #153) |
| \`per-pr-acceptance-contract.md\` | The template every rollout PR uses + main-branch post-merge audit checklist | (this PR uses it) |
| \`policy-ledgers.md\` | Orientation to \`policy/\` architecture, lifecycle, and per-ledger doc map | \`policy/README.md\` |

### JSON Schemas (\`contracts/schemas/\`)

| Schema | Validates | Producer | Consumer |
|---|---|---|---|
| \`ci-plan.v1.schema.json\` | \`target/ci/ci-plan.json\` | \`pr-plan.yml\` (PR #146); \`cargo xtask ci plan\` (PR #143) | GitHub Actions step summary; required-check (later) |
| \`ci-actuals.v1.schema.json\` | \`target/ci/ci-actuals.json\` | actuals collector (PR #148) | aggregator + drift report (later) |

Both schemas: \`schema_version = 1\`, additive-only forward compatibility (adding optional fields stays v1).

## Doctrine encoded

- **Every CI lane has one intent.** Duplicate intent declares \`duplicate_of\` (\`security.yml\` ↔ \`ci.yml#deny\` is the live example).
- **Definite skips, not pending.** Branch protection deadlocks come from undefined skip semantics; \`skipped-by-policy.md\` enumerates the 7 categories.
- **Bots are part of the CI economy.** Tracked under \`runner_multipliers.external_ai_review = 4.0\`; advisory unless GitGuardian critical or Droid \`block_on_critical\`.
- **Cache as architecture.** PRs restore from \`main\`-produced caches; PR-time saves are the wrong economy at agentic-PR volume.
- **Per-PR acceptance contract.** Self-binding receipt in every rollout PR description; this PR uses the template above.
- **Required-check migration.** Renames + removals in the same PR as the workflow change; additions can wait one cycle on \`main\`.

## Out of scope (deferred)

- ❌ \`xtask\` runner (lands in #143)
- ❌ \`pr-plan.yml\` workflow (lands in #146)
- ❌ Cache normalization implementation (lands in #147; this PR is the doc)
- ❌ CI actuals collector workflow (lands in #148)
- ❌ ripr workflow (lands in #153)
- ❌ Branch-protection actual changes (lands in #145 for MSRV rename, #146 for \`pr-plan / forecast\` add)

- [x] \`cargo fmt --all -- --check\` — clean
- [x] \`cargo check --workspace --all-targets --locked\` — clean (no Rust changes)
- [x] \`git diff --check\` — clean
- [ ] CI: \`ci.yml\` (\`check\` ubuntu + windows + \`deny\` + \`msrv\`) green
- [ ] CI: \`security.yml\`, \`property-testing.yml\`, all 4 \`bdd-testing.yml\` jobs, quick fuzz green
- [ ] CI: \`droid-review\` advisory; \`mutation-testing\` and extended fuzz correctly skipped
- [ ] Reviewer spot-checks: \`ci-lane-map.md\` (inventory + duplicates), \`per-pr-acceptance-contract.md\` (template), one of the two JSON Schemas

## Summary

PR #147 of the v0.5.0 ladder (Phase 4 — CI economics, 2/3). Sweeps \`Swatinem/rust-cache@v2\` to \`save-if: \${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' }}\` across the workspace's PR-time workflows so PRs **restore caches without fan-out** and \`main\` is the **canonical cache producer**. Adds \`paths-ignore\` to the compile-heavy non-required workflows so docs-only PRs don't pay their compile cost.

## PR acceptance contract

- **Scope:** cache-economics normalization + docs-only paths-ignore on non-required workflows
- **Files expected:** 5 workflow YAMLs (\`ci.yml\`, \`bdd-testing.yml\`, \`fuzzing.yml\`, \`mutation-testing.yml\`, \`property-testing.yml\`) + 2 doc updates (\`cache-policy.md\` status, \`rust-1.95-rollout.md\` status row) — 7 files
- **Behavior change:** yes (cache save behavior + docs-only path filtering on bdd/property/fuzz)
- **Advisory vs blocking:** none (no enforcement; cache change is performance/economy fix; paths-ignore only affects non-required workflows so branch protection is unaffected)
- **New artifacts:** none
- **Validation commands:**
  - \`cargo fmt --all -- --check\` → clean
  - \`cargo xtask check-policy-schemas\` → 18 ledgers OK
  - \`cargo xtask ci plan ...\` → emits 240 LEM plan (no behavior change in planner)
  - \`bash scripts/package-boundary-audit.sh\` → 22 + 2
  - \`bash scripts/package-version-audit.sh\` → 24 at 0.4.0
  - \`python -c "import yaml, glob; [yaml.safe_load(open(p)) for p in glob.glob('.github/workflows/*.yml')]"\` → all 12 workflows parse
  - \`git diff --check\` → clean
- **Rollback path:** \`git revert <merge-sha>\` — cache changes are additive (only \`save-if\` field added) so reverting brings back unconditional save; \`paths-ignore\` removal is also additive
- **Follow-up PR:** #148 (CI actuals — measures the actual LEM drop from these changes); #155 (broad lane routing — formalizes label/risk-pack routing on top of the docs-only skip already in place)

## What landed

### Cache normalization (12 sites across 5 workflows)

| Workflow | Sites | Cache pattern |
|---|---|---|
| \`ci.yml\` | 3 (check Ubuntu+Windows matrix, deny, msrv) | existing \`shared-key\` + new \`save-if: main\` |
| \`bdd-testing.yml\` | 5 (one per job) | distinct \`shared-key\` per job (bdd-testkit / bdd-ingest / bdd-render-trust / bdd-optional / bdd-app) + \`save-if: main\` |
| \`property-testing.yml\` | 1 | \`shared-key: property\` + \`save-if: main\` |
| \`fuzzing.yml\` | 2 (quick + extended) | \`shared-key: fuzz\` + \`save-if: main || schedule\` (so the daily extended-fuzz cron is also a producer) |
| \`mutation-testing.yml\` | 1 | \`shared-key: mutation\` + \`save-if: main || workflow_dispatch\` (so \`gh workflow run\` from main can refresh the cache) |

Already-correct workflows (no change needed):

- \`coverage.yml\` — has \`save-if: main\` already (per the v0.5 audit)
- \`pr-plan.yml\` — has \`save-if: main\` from PR #146
- \`release.yml\` — release-specific cache keys (\`release-preflight\` shared-key + per-target \`actions/cache\`); release events only, segregated from PR-fast keys

### Docs-only paths-ignore (3 non-required workflows)

| Workflow | Trigger | New filter |
|---|---|---|
| \`bdd-testing.yml\` | \`pull_request\` | skip \`docs/**\`, \`*.md\`, \`**/*.md\` |
| \`property-testing.yml\` | \`pull_request\` | skip \`docs/**\`, \`*.md\`, \`**/*.md\` |
| \`fuzzing.yml\` | \`pull_request\` (quick lane) | skip \`docs/**\`, \`*.md\`, \`**/*.md\` |

\`push\` and scheduled triggers are unchanged — \`main\` and nightly still run regardless of changed paths.

### Why ci.yml does NOT get paths-ignore

\`ci.yml\` has the workspace's required-merge gates (\`check\` Ubuntu + Windows, \`deny\`, \`msrv\` per [\`docs/ci/branch-protection.md\`](https://github.com/EffortlessMetrics/shiplog/blob/main/docs/ci/branch-protection.md)). A required check that doesn't run on a particular PR shows as \`pending\` in branch protection and deadlocks the merge.

The cache change still helps docs-only PRs on \`ci.yml\` — they restore from \`main\`'s warm cache without doing meaningful work, so wall-clock is small.

### Doc updates

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| \`docs/ci/cache-policy.md\` | Status of cache normalization moved from "PR #147 applies the pattern" to "PR #147 applied the pattern (now landed)"; docs-only skip section updated to reflect the partial application (skipping non-required only) and what runs on a docs-only PR post-#147 |
| \`docs/ci/rust-1.95-rollout.md\` | CI cache economics row: \`planned (PR #147)\` → \`landed (#147)\` |

## Out of scope (deferred)

- ❌ CI actuals collector (PR #148; closes the LEM feedback loop and measures the actual drop from these cache changes)
- ❌ ripr workflow (PR #153)
- ❌ Bounded stochastic / broad lane routing (PRs #154 + #155)
- ❌ Branch-protection changes
- ❌ Mutation routing changes (the cache change for mutation-testing.yml is internal to the same workflow; it doesn't change which lane runs when)
- ❌ Release version bump
- ❌ Budget enforcement

## Test plan

- [x] All local validation gates listed above
- [x] All 12 workflow YAMLs parse via \`yaml.safe_load\`
- [ ] CI: standard PR-fast lanes green
- [ ] CI: \`pr-plan / forecast\` green; emitted plan reflects no semantic change (still 240 LEM)
- [ ] Reviewer spot-checks: \`save-if\` value on each touched cache use; \`paths-ignore\` correctness on bdd/property/fuzz; \`ci.yml\` is unchanged for its triggers
- [ ] Post-merge on \`main\`: cache producer fires once per shared-key, refreshing each canonical cache

candidates.body:
## Summary

Adds 18 parse-only TOML policy ledgers + a \`policy/README.md\` orientation doc. This is **PR #141** of the v0.5.0 ladder (Phase 1 — machine-readable roadmap), per [\`docs/ci/rust-1.95-rollout.md\`](https://github.com/EffortlessMetrics/shiplog/blob/main/docs/ci/rust-1.95-rollout.md).

Skeletons seed obvious entries (existing 11 workflows, 9 release scripts, 22-crate workspace, current Clippy debt, Rust 1.95 lint floor) so later PRs read from declared contracts rather than inventing policy in code.

## PR acceptance contract

- **Scope:** machine-readable policy ledgers (parse-only)
- **Files expected:** \`policy/*.toml\` (18 files) + \`policy/README.md\` (1 file)
- **Behavior change:** no
- **Advisory vs blocking:** advisory (\`status = "advisory"\` in every ledger)
- **New artifacts:** 18 TOML ledgers + 1 orientation doc
- **Validation commands:**
  - \`python -c "import tomllib, glob; [tomllib.load(open(p,'rb')) for p in sorted(glob.glob('policy/*.toml'))]"\`
  - \`cargo fmt --all -- --check\`
  - \`cargo check --workspace --all-targets --locked\`
  - \`git diff --check\`
- **Rollback path:** \`git revert <merge-sha>\` — no enforcement to unwind, no Rust code touched
- **Follow-up PR:** #142 (CI operating-contract docs that reference these ledgers)

## Ledgers added

| Ledger | Entries | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| \`ci-budget.toml\` | budget tiers + 7 runner multipliers + 12 labels + external_cost_notes | LEM model |
| \`ci-lanes.toml\` | 18 lanes (11 existing workflows + planned pr_plan, ripr_advisory, mutation_targeted) | per-workflow lane assignments + duplicate_of |
| \`ci-risk-packs.toml\` | 12 named risk packs | path → label / lane routing |
| \`ci-exceptions.toml\` | 5 exceptions | Windows check parity, BDD/property/fuzz broad, droid review |
| \`clippy-lints.toml\` | 4 active + 16 planned | Rust 1.95 lint floor + Clippy ratchets, MSRV-gated |
| \`clippy-debt.toml\` | 3 broad workspace debt entries | needless_pass_by_value, cloned_instead_of_copied, missing_debug |
| \`clippy-exceptions.toml\` | skeleton + example | populated as \`#[expect(..., reason = "policy:...")]\` lands |
| \`no-panic-baseline.toml\` | skeleton | populated in #151 by \`cargo xtask no-panic baseline --reset\` |
| \`no-panic-allowlist.toml\` | skeleton + example | reserved for codified justified panic exceptions |
| \`non-rust-allowlist.toml\` | 24 allow entries | docs, workflows, scripts, fixtures, fuzz, git metadata |
| \`non-rust-debt.toml\` | skeleton + example | non-Rust files that should migrate to xtask |
| \`generated-allowlist.toml\` | skeleton | first entry added in #151 (no-panic-baseline.toml) |
| \`executable-allowlist.toml\` | 9 entries | the 9 existing executable scripts in scripts/ |
| \`workflow-allowlist.toml\` | 11 entries | one per .github/workflows/*.yml with permissions/secrets/external_actions |
| \`dependency-surface-allowlist.toml\` | 7 entries | Cargo files, lockfile, toolchain pin, deny config |
| \`process-allowlist.toml\` | 8 entries | cargo install, fuzz/mutation/llvm-cov, release scripts |
| \`network-allowlist.toml\` | 10 entries | crates.io, GitHub, Codecov, MiniMax, Factory, GitGuardian |
| \`ripr-suppressions.toml\` | skeleton + example | populated as findings are tracked starting in #153 |

Plus \`policy/README.md\` (orientation, common receipt fields, status, validation).

## Common receipt schema

Every ledger uses:

\`\`\`toml
schema_version = 1
policy = "<ledger-name>"
owner = "EffortlessMetrics"
status = "advisory"
\`\`\`

Every entry uses (per [\`docs/POLICY_ALLOWLISTS.md\`](https://github.com/EffortlessMetrics/shiplog/blob/main/docs/POLICY_ALLOWLISTS.md)):

\`\`\`toml
id = "<stable-identifier>"
owner = "<workspace-package or release|policy|ci|docs>"
reason = "<one-or-two-sentence explanation>"
created = "<ISO date>"
review_after = "<ISO date>"
expires = "<ISO date or 'permanent'>"
\`\`\`

Plus per-ledger extension fields (e.g. \`family\` + \`selector_kind\` for no-panic; \`permissions\` + \`external_actions\` for workflow).

## Out of scope (deferred)

Per the operating contract for #141:

- ❌ \`xtask\` runner (lands in #143)
- ❌ Workflow changes
- ❌ CI behavior changes
- ❌ Enforcement
- ❌ Rust code changes
- ❌ MSRV bump
- ❌ Operating-contract docs (lane-map.md, labels.md, risk-packs.md, branch-protection.md, required-check-migration.md, skipped-by-policy.md, bot-review-policy.md, cache-policy.md, ci-plan-json.md, ci-actuals.md, ripr.md, per-pr-acceptance-contract.md, policy-ledgers.md, contracts/schemas/ci-plan.v1.schema.json, contracts/schemas/ci-actuals.v1.schema.json) — all land in #142

## Test plan

- [x] Python tomllib parse: \`python -c "import tomllib, glob; [tomllib.load(open(p,'rb')) for p in sorted(glob.glob('policy/*.toml'))]"\` → all 18 parse OK
- [x] \`cargo fmt --all -- --check\` — clean
- [x] \`cargo check --workspace --all-targets --locked\` — clean (no Rust changes)
- [x] \`git diff --check\` — clean
- [ ] CI: \`ci.yml\` (\`check\` ubuntu + windows + \`deny\` + \`msrv\`) green
- [ ] CI: \`security.yml\`, \`property-testing.yml\`, all 4 \`bdd-testing.yml\` jobs, quick fuzz green
- [ ] CI: \`droid-review\` advisory; \`mutation-testing\` and extended fuzz correctly skipped
- [ ] Reviewer spot-checks one ledger per category: \`ci-lanes.toml\` (CI economics), \`clippy-lints.toml\` (Clippy doctrine), \`workflow-allowlist.toml\` (file policy)
